```
   178→def _collect_typed_dict_defs(
   179→    tree: ast.Module, accumulator: dict[str, set[str]]
   180→) -> None:
   181→    """Collect TypedDict class definitions from a single file's AST."""
   182→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   183→        if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   184→            continue
   185→        is_typed_dict = any(
   186→            (isinstance(b, ast.Name) and b.id == "TypedDict")
   187→            or (isinstance(b, ast.Attribute) and b.attr == "TypedDict")
   188→            for b in node.bases
   189→        )
   190→        if not is_typed_dict:
   191→            continue
   192→        fields: set[str] = set()
   193→        for child in node.body:
   194→            if isinstance(child, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(child.target, ast.Name):
   195→                fields.add(child.target.id)
   196→        if fields:
   197→            accumulator[node.name] = fields
   198→
   199→def _find_typed_dict_usage_violations(
   200→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module],
   201→    typed_dicts: dict[str, set[str]],
   202→) -> list[dict]:
   203→    """Find .get()/.setdefault()/.pop() calls on TypedDict-annotated variables.
   204→
   205→    *parsed_trees* maps absolute file paths to pre-parsed ASTs (built during
   206→    the main collection loop to avoid redundant parses).
   207→
   208→    Returns a list of violation dicts with file, typed_dict_name, violation_type,
   209→    line, field (when extractable), and count.
   210→    """
   211→    if not typed_dicts:
   212→        return []
   213→
   214→    violations: list[dict] = []
   215→    for filepath, tree in parsed_trees.items():
   216→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   217→
   218→        # Collect variable names annotated with known TypedDict types
   219→        typed_vars: dict[str, str] = {}  # var_name -> TypedDict name
   220→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   221→            if isinstance(node, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(node.target, ast.Name):
   222→                ann = node.annotation
   223→                ann_name = None
   224→                if isinstance(ann, ast.Name):
   225→                    ann_name = ann.id
   226→                elif isinstance(ann, ast.Attribute):
   227→                    ann_name = ann.attr
   228→                if ann_name in typed_dicts:
   229→                    typed_vars[node.target.id] = ann_name
   230→            # Also check function param annotations
   231→            if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   232→                for arg in node.args.args + node.args.kwonlyargs:
   233→                    ann = arg.annotation
   234→                    if ann is None:
   235→                        continue
   236→                    ann_name = None
   237→                    if isinstance(ann, ast.Name):
   238→                        ann_name = ann.id
   239→                    elif isinstance(ann, ast.Attribute):
   240→                        ann_name = ann.attr
   241→                    if ann_name in typed_dicts:
   242→                        typed_vars[arg.arg] = ann_name
   243→
   244→        if not typed_vars:
   245→            continue
   246→
   247→        # Scan for violation calls — collect per (td_name, method, field)
   248→        hits: list[tuple[str, str, str | None, int]] = []
   249→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   250→            if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
   251→                continue
   252→            func = node.func
   253→            if not isinstance(func, ast.Attribute):
   254→                continue
   255→            if func.attr not in _VIOLATION_METHODS:
   256→                continue
   257→            if not isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) or func.value.id not in typed_vars:
   258→                continue
   259→            td_name = typed_vars[func.value.id]
   260→            # Extract the field name from the first argument if it's a string constant
   261→            field: str | None = None
   262→            if node.args and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Constant):
   263→                val = node.args[0].value
   264→                if isinstance(val, str):
   265→                    field = val
   266→            hits.append((td_name, func.attr, field, node.lineno))
   267→
   268→        # Group by (td_name, method, field) for compact reporting
   269→        groups: dict[tuple[str, str, str | None], list[int]] = {}
   270→        for td_name, method, field, lineno in hits:
   271→            groups.setdefault((td_name, method, field), []).append(lineno)
   272→
   273→        for (td_name, method, field), lines in groups.items():
   274→            entry: dict = {
   275→                "file": rpath,
   276→                "typed_dict_name": td_name,
   277→                "violation_type": method,
   278→                "line": lines[0],
   279→                "count": len(lines),
   280→            }
   281→            if field is not None:
   282→                entry["field"] = field
   283→            violations.append(entry)
   284→
   285→    return violations
   286→
   287→
   288→# ── dict[str, Any] annotation scanner ─────────────────────
   289→
   290→
   291→def _find_dict_any_annotations(
   292→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module],
   293→    typed_dict_names: set[str],
   294→) -> list[dict]:
   295→    """Find function parameters/returns annotated as ``dict[str, Any]``.
   296→
   297→    Cross-references parameter names against known TypedDict names to suggest
   298→    concrete alternatives when available.
   299→    """
   300→    results: list[dict] = []
   301→    for filepath, tree in parsed_trees.items():
   302→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   303→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   304→            if not isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
   305→                continue
   306→            # Check args
   307→            for arg in node.args.args + node.args.kwonlyargs:
   308→                if arg.annotation and _is_dict_str_any(arg.annotation):
   309→                    alt = _guess_alternative(arg.arg, typed_dict_names)
   310→                    results.append({
   311→                        "file": rpath,
   312→                        "function": node.name,
   313→                        "param": arg.arg,
   314→                        "line": arg.lineno,
   315→                        "known_alternative": alt,
   316→                    })
   317→            # Check return annotation
   318→            if node.returns and _is_dict_str_any(node.returns):
   319→                results.append({
   320→                    "file": rpath,
   321→                    "function": node.name,
   322→                    "param": "(return)",
   323→                    "line": node.lineno,
   324→                    "known_alternative": None,
   325→                })
   326→    return results
   327→
   328→
   329→def _is_dict_str_any(ann: ast.expr) -> bool:
   330→    """Check if annotation is ``dict[str, Any]``."""
   331→    if not isinstance(ann, ast.Subscript):
   332→        return False
   333→    if not (isinstance(ann.value, ast.Name) and ann.value.id == "dict"):
   334→        return False
   335→    sl = ann.slice
   336→    if isinstance(sl, ast.Tuple) and len(sl.elts) == 2:
   337→        first, second = sl.elts
   338→        if isinstance(first, ast.Name) and first.id == "str":
   339→            if isinstance(second, ast.Name) and second.id == "Any":
   340→                return True
   341→    return False
   342→
   343→
   344→def _guess_alternative(param_name: str, typed_dict_names: set[str]) -> str | None:
   345→    """Guess a TypedDict alternative by matching param name fragments."""
   346→    lower = param_name.lower()
   347→    for td_name in sorted(typed_dict_names):
   348→        if td_name.lower() in lower or lower in td_name.lower():
   349→            return td_name
   350→    return None
   351→
   352→
   353→# ── Enum bypass scanner ───────────────────────────────────
   354→
   355→
   356→def _collect_enum_defs(
   357→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module],
   358→) -> dict[str, dict]:
   359→    """Find StrEnum/IntEnum/Enum class defs.
   360→
   361→    Returns ``{name: {file, members: {name: value}}}``.
   362→    """
   363→    _ENUM_BASES = {"StrEnum", "IntEnum", "Enum"}
   364→    result: dict[str, dict] = {}
   365→    for filepath, tree in parsed_trees.items():
   366→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   367→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   368→            if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   369→                continue
   370→            is_enum = any(
   371→                (isinstance(b, ast.Name) and b.id in _ENUM_BASES)
   372→                or (isinstance(b, ast.Attribute) and b.attr in _ENUM_BASES)
   373→                for b in node.bases
   374→            )
   375→            if not is_enum:
   376→                continue
   377→            members: dict[str, object] = {}
   378→            for child in node.body:
   379→                if isinstance(child, ast.Assign):
   380→                    for target in child.targets:
   381→                        if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and isinstance(
   382→                            child.value, ast.Constant
   383→                        ):
   384→                            members[target.id] = child.value.value
   385→            if members:
   386→                result[node.name] = {"file": rpath, "members": members}
   387→    return result
   388→
   389→
   390→def _find_enum_bypass(
   391→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module],
   392→    enum_defs: dict[str, dict],
   393→) -> list[dict]:
   394→    """Find raw string/int comparisons that match enum member values."""
   395→    if not enum_defs:
   396→        return []
   397→
   398→    # Build reverse lookup: value → (enum_name, member_name)
   399→    value_to_enum: dict[object, tuple[str, str]] = {}
   400→    for enum_name, info in enum_defs.items():
   401→        for member_name, value in info["members"].items():
   402→            if isinstance(value, (str, int)):
   403→                value_to_enum[value] = (enum_name, member_name)
   404→
   405→    if not value_to_enum:
   406→        return []
   407→
   408→    results: list[dict] = []
   409→    for filepath, tree in parsed_trees.items():
   410→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   411→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   412→            if not isinstance(node, ast.Compare):
   413→                continue
   414→            # Check all comparators (left + comparators)
   415→            for const_node in [node.left, *node.comparators]:
   416→                if not isinstance(const_node, ast.Constant):
   417→                    continue
   418→                [REDACTED]
   419→                if key in value_to_enum:
   420→                    enum_name, member = value_to_enum[key]
   421→                    results.append({
   422→                        "file": rpath,
   423→                        "line": node.lineno,
   424→                        "enum_name": enum_name,
   425→                        "member": member,
   426→                        "raw_value": repr(key),
   427→                    })
   428→    return results
   429→
   430→
   431→# ── Type strategy census ──────────────────────────────────
   432→
   433→
   434→def _census_type_strategies(
   435→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module],
   436→) -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
   437→    """Count domain object definitions by strategy.
   438→
   439→    Returns ``{strategy: [{name, file, field_count}]}``.
   440→    """
   441→    strategies: dict[str, list[dict]] = {
   442→        "TypedDict": [],
   443→        "dataclass": [],
   444→        "frozen_dataclass": [],
   445→        "NamedTuple": [],
   446→    }
   447→    for filepath, tree in parsed_trees.items():
   448→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   449→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   450→            if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   451→                continue
   452→            field_count = sum(
   453→                1 for c in node.body if isinstance(c, ast.AnnAssign)
   454→            )
   455→            entry = {"name": node.name, "file": rpath, "field_count": field_count}
   456→
   457→            # TypedDict
   458→            if any(
   459→                (isinstance(b, ast.Name) and b.id == "TypedDict")
   460→                or (isinstance(b, ast.Attribute) and b.attr == "TypedDict")
   461→                for b in node.bases
   462→            ):
   463→                strategies["TypedDict"].append(entry)
   464→                continue
   465→
   466→            # NamedTuple
   467→            if any(
   468→                (isinstance(b, ast.Name) and b.id == "NamedTuple")
   469→                or (isinstance(b, ast.Attribute) and b.attr == "NamedTuple")
   470→                for b in node.bases
   471→            ):
   472→                strategies["NamedTuple"].append(entry)
   473→                continue
   474→
   475→            # dataclass (check decorators)
   476→            for dec in node.decorator_list:
   477→                is_dc = False
   478→                is_frozen = False
   479→                if isinstance(dec, ast.Name) and dec.id == "dataclass":
   480→                    is_dc = True
   481→                elif isinstance(dec, ast.Attribute) and dec.attr == "dataclass":
   482→                    is_dc = True
   483→                elif isinstance(dec, ast.Call):
   484→                    func = dec.func
   485→                    if (isinstance(func, ast.Name) and func.id == "dataclass") or (
   486→                        isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr == "dataclass"
   487→                    ):
   488→                        is_dc = True
   489→                        # Check for frozen=True
   490→                        for kw in dec.keywords:
   491→                            if (
   492→                                kw.arg == "frozen"
   493→                                and isinstance(kw.value, ast.Constant)
   494→                                and kw.value.value is True
   495→                            ):
   496→                                is_frozen = True
   497→                if is_dc:
   498→                    [REDACTED] if is_frozen else "dataclass"
   499→                    strategies[key].append(entry)
   500→                    break
   501→
   502→    # Remove empty strategies
   503→    return {k: v for k, v in strategies.items() if v}
   504→
   505→
   506→__all__ = [
   507→    "_census_type_strategies",
   508→    "_collect_enum_defs",
   509→    "_collect_typed_dict_defs",
   510→    "_find_delegation_heavy_classes",
   511→    "_find_dict_any_annotations",
   512→    "_find_enum_bypass",
   513→    "_find_facade_modules",
   514→    "_find_python_passthrough_wrappers",
   515→    "_find_typed_dict_usage_violations",
   516→    "_is_delegation_stmt",
   517→    "_python_passthrough_target",
   518→]
```

```
1→"""Shared helpers for language-specific re-export facade detectors."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from collections.abc import Callable
     6→
     7→
     8→def _facade_tier_confidence(importer_count: int) -> tuple[int, str]:
     9→    """Determine tier and confidence for a facade based on importer count.
    10→
    11→    ≤5 importers: tier 2, confidence high   (easy removal)
    12→    6-20 importers: tier 3, confidence medium (moderate effort)
    13→    >20 importers: tier 4, confidence medium  (large-scale refactor)
    14→    """
    15→    if importer_count <= 5:
    16→        return 2, "high"
    17→    if importer_count <= 20:
    18→        return 3, "medium"
    19→    return 4, "medium"
    20→
    21→
    22→def detect_reexport_facades_common(
    23→    graph: dict,
    24→    *,
    25→    is_facade_fn: Callable[[str], dict | None],
    26→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    27→    """Collect file-level re-export facades using a language detector callback.
    28→
    29→    All pure re-export facades are reported regardless of importer count.
    30→    Tier is based on removal difficulty.
    31→    """
    32→    entries: list[dict] = []
    33→    total_checked = 0
    34→
    35→    for filepath, node in graph.items():
    36→        total_checked += 1
    37→
    38→        result = is_facade_fn(filepath)
    39→        if not result:
    40→            continue
    41→
    42→        importer_count = node.get("importer_count", 0)
    43→        tier, confidence = _facade_tier_confidence(importer_count)
    44→
    45→        entries.append(
    46→            {
    47→                "file": filepath,
    48→                "loc": result["loc"],
    49→                "importers": importer_count,
    50→                "imports_from": result["imports_from"],
    51→                "kind": "file",
    52→                "tier": tier,
    53→                "confidence": confidence,
    54→            }
    55→        )
    56→
    57→    return entries, total_checked
    58→
    59→
    60→__all__ = [
    61→    "_facade_tier_confidence",
    62→    "detect_reexport_facades_common",
    63→]
    64→
```

So `not _is_mutable_literal(X)` at this code point is equivalent to `not isinstance(X, _MUTABLE_INIT + (ast.Call,))`, or more simply `isinstance(X, ast.Constant)`.

Now the zero/negative values test. The old test used `{"signals": {"max_params": 0, "max_nesting": -1, "loc": 0}}`. With the flat format, `loc: 0` is directly in detail, and for params/nesting we use complexity_signals strings. But `0 params` and negative nesting won't be produced by real code -- they're edge cases. Since `_update_max_signal` ignores values <= 0, and `_parse_complexity_signals` uses regex to extract numbers, a `"0 params"` string would parse to 0 which `_update_max_signal` would reject. Let me think about what the test actually tests: it verifies that zero and negative values are ignored. With the flat format:

- `loc: 0` -> `_update_max_signal` ignores it (value <= 0)
- `"0 params"` -> parsed as 0, `_update_max_signal` ignores it
- Negative nesting can't really be expressed in string format, but we can test with `loc: -1` in the flat dict

## Changes to `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/intelligence/review/context_holistic/budget_patterns.py`

### Fix 1: Only flag `==` and `!=` operators

In `_find_enum_bypass`, added a guard that checks `node.ops` and skips the comparison if any operator is not `ast.Eq` or `ast.NotEq`:

```python
# Only flag == and != operators.
if not all(isinstance(op, (ast.Eq, ast.NotEq)) for op in node.ops):
    continue
```

This prevents flagging `x > "active"` or `x < 1` as enum bypass.

### Fix 2: Skip generic int literals

Added a module-level constant:

```python
_GENERIC_INT_VALUES: frozenset[object] = frozenset({0, 1, 2, 3, -1, True, False})
```

In `_find_enum_bypass`, the reverse-lookup builder now only adds int values that are NOT in this set:

```python
elif isinstance(value, int) and value not in _GENERIC_INT_VALUES:
    value_to_enums.setdefault(value, []).append((enum_name, member_name))
```

### Fix 3: Skip the enum's own definition file

`_find_enum_bypass` now collects the set of files that define enums and skips them during scanning:

```python
enum_def_files: set[str] = {info["file"] for info in enum_defs.values()}
# ...
if rpath in enum_def_files:
    continue
```

### Fix 4: `_collect_enum_defs` keyed by `(file, name)` instead of just name

Changed the return type from `dict[str, dict]` to `dict[tuple[str, str], dict]`. The key is now `(rpath, class_name)`, so same-named enums from different files are both preserved instead of silently overwritten.

### Fix 5: `value_to_enum` last-write-wins resolved

Changed from a single-value dict (`value_to_enum: dict[object, tuple[str, str]]`) to a list-based dict (`value_to_enums: dict[object, list[tuple[str, str]]]`). When two enums share a member value, all mappings are preserved and each generates a separate result entry.

All 25 mutable state tests pass as well. Here is a summary of all the changes made:

---

## Summary of Changes

### Fix 1: `unused_enums.py` name collision bug
**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/python/detectors/unused_enums.py`

Changed `all_enum_names` from `dict[str, str]` (name -> single defining file) to `dict[str, list[str]]` (name -> list of defining files). Used `.setdefault(d["name"], []).append(filepath)` instead of simple assignment. Updated the cross-reference check to use `filepath not in all_enum_names[name]` instead of `all_enum_names[name] != filepath`, so an enum is considered "externally imported" if any file other than its defining files imports it. This prevents a second file defining `class Status(StrEnum)` from silently overwriting the first.

### Fix 2: Dead code `_is_mutable_literal()`
**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/python/detectors/mutable_state.py`

Removed the `_is_mutable_literal()` function (lines 55-65). The two call sites on lines 81 and 92 used it within a branch where `_is_mutable_init()` had already returned True, meaning the value was either a mutable literal (`ast.List`/`ast.Dict`/`ast.Set`/`ast.Call`) or `ast.Constant(None)`. The check `not _is_mutable_literal(X)` in that context is equivalent to `isinstance(X, ast.Constant)`, which is the replacement used.

### Fix 3: `_detect_del_param` docstring stripping
**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/python/detectors/smells_ast/_tree_quality_detectors.py`

Added docstring stripping before checking the first 3 body statements, matching the pattern already used in `_detect_noop_function()` in the same file. `_is_docstring` was already imported from `._helpers` (line 8). The new code:
```python
body = node.body
if body and _is_docstring(body[0]):
    body = body[1:]
for stmt in body[:3]:
    ...
```
This ensures that a function with a docstring + 3 real statements correctly examines all 3 real statements instead of only 2.

### Fix 4: `_find_dict_any_annotations` missing `posonlyargs`
**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/intelligence/review/context_holistic/budget_patterns.py`

Changed the arg iteration from `node.args.args + node.args.kwonlyargs` to `node.args.posonlyargs + node.args.args + node.args.kwonlyargs` so positional-only parameters (those before `/` in the signature) are also checked for `dict[str, Any]` annotations.

### Fix 5: `_guess_alternative` false matches for short names
**File:** `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/intelligence/review/context_holistic/budget_patterns.py`

Added an early return `if len(param_name) < 4: return None` to prevent single/two/three-letter parameter names like `"d"` from falsely matching TypedDict names like `"SomeDict"`. Also changed the function to collect all matches and return `None` when multiple TypedDicts match (ambiguous), only returning a suggestion when exactly one TypedDict matches.

### Test verification
All 55 tests in the three specified test files pass, plus all 25 mutable state tests pass, confirming the changes are correct. The existing `test_del_param_at_boundary_third_stmt` test did not need updating since its test function has no docstring.

So `_get_signals()` is called on the issue and then `.get("max_params")`, `.get("max_nesting")`, `.get("loc")`, `.get("complexity_score")`, `.get("function_count")`, `.get("component_count")` are read from it. 

When we have `detail={"signals": {"loc": 1000, "max_params": 8, ...}}`, `_get_signals()` returns `{"loc": 1000, "max_params": 8, ...}` (the nested dict).

When we change to `detail={"loc": 1000, "max_params": 8, ...}` (flat), `_get_signals()` will check `detail.get("signals")` which is `None`, so it falls back to returning `detail` itself: `{"loc": 1000, "max_params": 8, ...}`. This works identically.

```
   110→def _parse_complexity_signals(detail: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, float]:
   111→    """Parse complexity_signals strings into numeric values.
   112→
   113→    Structural detail dicts store complexity signals as strings like
   114→    "12 params" and "nesting depth 8" in the ``complexity_signals``
   115→    list.  Extract max_params and max_nesting from those labels so
   116→    the concern generator can evaluate thresholds.
   117→    """
   118→    result: dict[str, float] = {}
   119→    raw_signals = detail.get("complexity_signals", [])
   120→    if not isinstance(raw_signals, list):
   121→        return result
   122→
   123→    for sig in raw_signals:
   124→        if not isinstance(sig, str):
   125→            continue
   126→        m = re.search(r"(\d+)\s*params", sig)
   127→        if m:
   128→            result["max_params"] = max(result.get("max_params", 0), float(m.group(1)))
   129→        m = re.search(r"nesting depth\s*(\d+)", sig)
   130→        if m:
   131→            result["max_nesting"] = max(result.get("max_nesting", 0), float(m.group(1)))
   132→    return result
   133→
   134→
   135→def _extract_signals(issues: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> ConcernSignals:
   136→    """Extract key quantitative signals from a file's issues."""
   137→    signals: ConcernSignals = {}
   138→    monster_funcs: list[str] = []
   139→
   140→    for f in issues:
   141→        det = f.get("detector", "")
   142→        detail_raw = f.get("detail", {})
   143→        detail = detail_raw if isinstance(detail_raw, dict) else {}
   144→
   145→        if det == "structural":
   146→            # Read loc directly from the flat detail dict.
   147→            _update_max_signal(signals, "loc", detail.get("loc", 0))
   148→            # Parse complexity_signals strings for params/nesting.
   149→            parsed = _parse_complexity_signals(detail)
   150→            for key in ("max_params", "max_nesting"):
   151→                if key in parsed:
   152→                    _update_max_signal(signals, cast(SignalKey, key), parsed[key])
   153→
   154→        if det == "smells" and detail.get("smell_id") == "monster_function":
   155→            _update_max_signal(signals, "monster_loc", detail.get("loc", 0))
   156→            func = detail.get("function", "")
   157→            if isinstance(func, str) and func:
   158→                monster_funcs.append(func)
   159→
   160→    if monster_funcs:
   161→        signals["monster_funcs"] = monster_funcs
   162→    return signals
```

```
    37→

    41→                "function with 10 params",
```

```
1→"""Metadata and logging mutations for plan operations."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import ExecutionLogEntry, PlanModel, ensure_plan_defaults
     6→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import utc_now
     7→
     8→_DEFAULT_MAX_LOG_ENTRIES = 10000
     9→
    10→
    11→def _get_log_cap() -> int:
    12→    """Read execution_log_max_entries from config. Returns 0 for unlimited."""
    13→    try:
    14→        from desloppify.core.config import load_config
    15→
    16→        config = load_config()
    17→        value = config.get("execution_log_max_entries", _DEFAULT_MAX_LOG_ENTRIES)
    18→        return max(0, int(value))
    19→    except (ImportError, OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
    20→        return _DEFAULT_MAX_LOG_ENTRIES
    21→
    22→
    23→def append_log_entry(
    24→    plan: PlanModel,
    25→    action: str,
    26→    *,
    27→    issue_ids: list[str] | None = None,
    28→    cluster_name: str | None = None,
    29→    actor: str = "user",
    30→    note: str | None = None,
    31→    detail: dict | None = None,
    32→) -> None:
    33→    """Append a structured entry to the plan's execution log."""
    34→    log = plan.get("execution_log", [])
    35→    entry: ExecutionLogEntry = {
    36→        "timestamp": utc_now(),
    37→        "action": action,
    38→        "issue_ids": issue_ids or [],
    39→        "cluster_name": cluster_name,
    40→        "actor": actor,
    41→        "note": note,
    42→        "detail": detail or {},
    43→    }
    44→    log.append(entry)
    45→    cap = _get_log_cap()
    46→    if cap > 0 and len(log) > cap:
    47→        plan["execution_log"] = log[-cap:]
    48→
    49→
    50→def describe_issue(
    51→    plan: PlanModel, issue_id: str, description: str | None
    52→) -> None:
    53→    """Set or clear an augmented description on a issue."""
    54→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    55→    now = utc_now()
    56→    overrides = plan["overrides"]
    57→    if issue_id not in overrides:
    58→        overrides[issue_id] = {"issue_id": issue_id, "created_at": now}
    59→    overrides[issue_id]["description"] = description
    60→    overrides[issue_id]["updated_at"] = now
    61→
    62→
    63→def annotate_issue(
    64→    plan: PlanModel, issue_id: str, note: str | None
    65→) -> None:
    66→    """Set or clear a note on a issue."""
    67→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
    68→    now = utc_now()
    69→    overrides = plan["overrides"]
    70→    if issue_id not in overrides:
    71→        overrides[issue_id] = {"issue_id": issue_id, "created_at": now}
    72→    overrides[issue_id]["note"] = note
    73→    overrides[issue_id]["updated_at"] = now
    74→
    75→
    76→__all__ = ["annotate_issue", "append_log_entry", "describe_issue"]
```

I've identified the root causes for all 9 test failures. **These are NOT related to your plan implementation changes** — they are **pre-existing test infrastructure issues** from other recent changes in the branch:

The new `operations.py` is now a facade that re-exports functions, but it does **not** re-export the private `_get_log_cap()` function (by design). The tests try to monkeypatch `desloppify.engine._plan.operations._get_log_cap`, which no longer exists at that path.

```
   351→def _file_concerns(state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Concern]:
   352→    """Per-file design concerns from aggregated mechanical signals.
   353→
   354→    Flags a file if it has 2+ judgment-needed detectors OR a single
   355→    detector with elevated signals (monster function, high params,
   356→    deep nesting, duplication, coupling, mixed responsibilities).
   357→    Bundles ALL issues for that file so the LLM sees the full picture.
   358→    """
   359→    by_file = _group_by_file(state)
   360→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   361→
   362→    for file, all_issues in by_file.items():
   363→        judgment = [
   364→            f for f in all_issues
   365→            if f.get("detector", "") in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   366→        ]
   367→        if not judgment:
   368→            continue
   369→
   370→        judgment_dets = {f.get("detector", "") for f in judgment}
   371→        elevated = _has_elevated_signals(judgment)
   372→
   373→        # Flag if 2+ judgment detectors OR 1 with elevated signals
   374→        # OR 1 judgment detector + 2 mechanical issues from any detector.
   375→        mechanical_count = len(all_issues)
   376→        if len(judgment_dets) < 2 and not elevated:
   377→            if not (len(judgment_dets) >= 1 and mechanical_count >= 3):
   378→                continue
   379→
   380→        signals = _extract_signals(judgment)
   381→        concern_type = _classify(judgment_dets, signals)
   382→        evidence = _build_evidence(judgment, signals)
   383→        question = _build_question(judgment_dets, signals)
   384→        summary = _build_summary(concern_type, judgment_dets, signals)
   385→
   386→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(f.get("id", "") for f in judgment))
   387→        fp_keys = tuple(sorted(judgment_dets))
   388→        fp = _fingerprint(concern_type, file, fp_keys)
   389→
   390→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   391→            continue
   392→
   393→        concerns.append(
   394→            Concern(
   395→                type=concern_type,
   396→                file=file,
   397→                summary=summary,
   398→                evidence=evidence,
   399→                question=question,
   400→                fingerprint=fp,
   401→                source_issues=all_ids,
   402→            )
   403→        )
   404→
   405→    return concerns
   406→
   407→
   408→def _cross_file_patterns(state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]) -> list[Concern]:
   409→    """Systemic patterns: same judgment detector combo across 3+ files.
   410→
   411→    When multiple files share the same combination of detector types,
   412→    that's likely a codebase-wide pattern rather than isolated issues.
   413→    """
   414→    by_file = _group_by_file(state)
   415→
   416→    # Group files by their judgment detector profile.
   417→    profile_to_files: dict[frozenset[str], list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   418→    for file, issues in by_file.items():
   419→        dets = frozenset(
   420→            f.get("detector", "") for f in issues
   421→            if f.get("detector", "") in JUDGMENT_DETECTORS
   422→        )
   423→        if len(dets) >= 2:
   424→            profile_to_files[dets].append(file)
   425→
   426→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   427→    for det_combo, files in profile_to_files.items():
   428→        if len(files) < MIN_FILES_FOR_SYSTEMIC:
   429→            continue
   430→
   431→        sorted_files = sorted(files)
   432→        combo_names = tuple(sorted(det_combo))
   433→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(
   434→            f.get("id", "")
   435→            for file in sorted_files
   436→            for f in by_file[file]
   437→            if f.get("detector", "") in det_combo
   438→        ))
   439→        # Use first few files in fingerprint so it's stable but bounded.
   440→        fp = _fingerprint(
   441→            "systemic_pattern",
   442→            ",".join(sorted_files[:5]),
   443→            combo_names,
   444→        )
   445→
   446→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   447→            continue
   448→
   449→        concerns.append(
   450→            Concern(
   451→                type="systemic_pattern",
   452→                file=sorted_files[0],
   453→                summary=(
   454→                    f"{len(files)} files share the same problem pattern "
   455→                    f"({', '.join(combo_names)})"
   456→                ),
   457→                evidence=(
   458→                    f"Affected files: {', '.join(sorted_files[:10])}",
   459→                    f"Shared detectors: {', '.join(combo_names)}",
   460→                    f"Total files: {len(files)}",
   461→                ),
   462→                question=(
   463→                    f"These {len(files)} files all have the same combination "
   464→                    f"of issues ({', '.join(combo_names)}). Is this a systemic "
   465→                    "pattern that should be addressed at the architecture level "
   466→                    "(shared base class, framework change, lint rule), or are "
   467→                    "these independent issues that happen to look similar?"
   468→                ),
   469→                fingerprint=fp,
   470→                source_issues=all_ids,
   471→            )
   472→        )
   473→
   474→    return concerns
   475→
   476→
   477→def _systemic_smell_patterns(
   478→    state: StateModel, dismissals: dict[str, Any]
   479→) -> list[Concern]:
   480→    """Systemic concerns: single smell_id appearing across 5+ files.
   481→
   482→    Complements _cross_file_patterns which looks at detector-combo profiles.
   483→    This catches pervasive single-smell issues (e.g. broad_except in 12 files).
   484→    """
   485→    smell_files: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   486→    smell_ids_map: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)  # smell_id -> issue IDs
   487→
   488→    for f in _open_issues(state):
   489→        if f.get("detector") != "smells":
   490→            continue
   491→        detail = f.get("detail", {})
   492→        smell_id = detail.get("smell_id", "") if isinstance(detail, dict) else ""
   493→        filepath = f.get("file", "")
   494→        if smell_id and filepath and filepath != ".":
   495→            smell_files[smell_id].append(filepath)
   496→            smell_ids_map[smell_id].append(f.get("id", ""))
   497→
   498→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   499→    for smell_id, files in smell_files.items():
   500→        unique_files = sorted(set(files))
   501→        if len(unique_files) < MIN_FILES_FOR_SMELL_PATTERN:
   502→            continue
   503→
   504→        all_ids = tuple(sorted(smell_ids_map[smell_id]))
   505→        fp = _fingerprint("systemic_smell", smell_id, (smell_id,))
   506→        if _is_dismissed(dismissals, fp, all_ids):
   507→            continue
   508→
   509→        concerns.append(
   510→            Concern(
   511→                type="systemic_smell",
   512→                file=unique_files[0],
   513→                summary=(
   514→                    f"'{smell_id}' appears in {len(unique_files)} files — "
   515→                    "likely a systemic pattern"
   516→                ),
   517→                evidence=(
   518→                    f"Smell: {smell_id}",
   519→                    f"Affected files ({len(unique_files)}): {', '.join(unique_files[:10])}",
   520→                ),
   521→                question=(
   522→                    f"The smell '{smell_id}' appears across {len(unique_files)} files. "
   523→                    "Is this a codebase-wide convention that should be addressed "
   524→                    "systemically (lint rule, shared utility, architecture change), "
   525→                    "or are these independent occurrences?"
   526→                ),
   527→                fingerprint=fp,
   528→                source_issues=all_ids,
   529→            )
   530→        )
   531→
   532→    return concerns
   533→
   534→
   535→_GENERATORS = [_file_concerns, _cross_file_patterns, _systemic_smell_patterns]
   536→
   537→
   538→def generate_concerns(
   539→    state: StateModel,
   540→) -> list[Concern]:
   541→    """Run all concern generators against current state.
   542→
   543→    Returns deduplicated list sorted by (type, file).
   544→    """
   545→    dismissals = state.get("concern_dismissals", {})
   546→    concerns: list[Concern] = []
   547→    seen_fps: set[str] = set()
   548→
   549→    for gen in _GENERATORS:
   550→        for concern in gen(state, dismissals):
   551→            if concern.fingerprint not in seen_fps:
   552→                seen_fps.add(concern.fingerprint)
   553→                concerns.append(concern)
   554→
   555→    concerns.sort(key=lambda c: (c.type, c.file))
   556→    return concerns
   557→
   558→
   559→def cleanup_stale_dismissals(state: StateModel) -> int:
   560→    """Remove dismissals whose source issues all disappeared.
   561→
   562→    Returns the number of stale entries removed.  Dismissals without
   563→    ``source_issue_ids`` (legacy) are left untouched.
   564→    """
   565→    dismissals = state.get("concern_dismissals", {})
   566→    if not dismissals:
   567→        return 0
   568→    open_ids = {f.get("id", "") for f in _open_issues(state)}
   569→    stale_fps = [
   570→        fp
   571→        for fp, entry in dismissals.items()
   572→        if entry.get("source_issue_ids")
   573→        and not any(sid in open_ids for sid in entry["source_issue_ids"])
   574→    ]
   575→    for fp in stale_fps:
   576→        del dismissals[fp]
   577→    return len(stale_fps)
   578→
   579→
   580→__all__ = ["Concern", "cleanup_stale_dismissals", "generate_concerns"]
   581→
```

```
    15→def _python_passthrough_target(stmt: ast.stmt) -> str | None:
    16→    """Return passthrough call target when stmt is `return target(...)`."""
    17→    if not isinstance(stmt, ast.Return):
    18→        return None
    19→    value = stmt.value
    20→    if not isinstance(value, ast.Call):
    21→        return None
    22→    target = value.func
    23→    if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
    24→        return target.id
    25→    return None
    26→
    27→def _find_python_passthrough_wrappers(tree: ast.Module) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
    28→    """Find Python wrapper pairs via AST traversal."""
    29→    wrappers: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
    30→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
    31→        if not isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
    32→            continue
    33→
    34→        body = _strip_docstring(list(node.body))
    35→        if len(body) != 1:
    36→            continue
    37→
    38→        target_name = _python_passthrough_target(body[0])
    39→        if target_name and node.name != target_name:
    40→            wrappers.append((node.name, target_name))
    41→    return wrappers
    42→
    43→def _is_delegation_stmt(stmt: ast.stmt) -> str | None:
    44→    """Return the delegate attribute name if *stmt* is a pure delegation.
    45→
    46→    Matches patterns like:
    47→    - ``return self.x.method(...)``
    48→    - ``return self.x``  (property forwarding)
    49→    - ``self.x.method(...)``  (void delegation)
    50→    """
    51→    # Unwrap Expr nodes (void calls like ``self.x.do()``)
    52→    if isinstance(stmt, ast.Expr):
    53→        value = stmt.value
    54→    elif isinstance(stmt, ast.Return) and stmt.value is not None:
    55→        value = stmt.value
    56→    else:
    57→        return None
    58→
    59→    # ``self.x.method(...)`` or ``self.x(...)``
    60→    if isinstance(value, ast.Call):
    61→        value = value.func
    62→
    63→    # Walk the attribute chain to find ``self.<attr>``
    64→    node = value
    65→    depth = 0
    66→    while isinstance(node, ast.Attribute):
    67→        node = node.value
    68→        depth += 1
    69→    if depth < 1 or not isinstance(node, ast.Name) or node.id != "self":
    70→        return None
    71→
    72→    # The first attribute after self — walk back down from the outermost
    73→    # Attribute to find the one whose .value is the Name("self") node.
    74→    first = value
    75→    while isinstance(first, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(first.value, ast.Attribute):
    76→        first = first.value
    77→    if isinstance(first, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(first.value, ast.Name):
    78→        return first.attr
    79→    return None

    81→def _find_delegation_heavy_classes(tree: ast.Module) -> list[dict]:
    82→    """Find classes where most methods delegate to a single inner object."""
    83→    results: list[dict] = []
    84→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
    85→        if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
    86→            continue
    87→
    88→        methods: list[ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef] = [
    89→            child
    90→            for child in node.body
    91→            if isinstance(child, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef)
    92→            and child.name != "__init__"
    93→        ]
    94→        if len(methods) <= 3:
    95→            continue
    96→
    97→        # Track which methods delegate to which attribute
    98→        delegating_methods: dict[str, list[str]] = {}  # attr -> [method_names]
    99→        for method in methods:
   100→            body = _strip_docstring(list(method.body))
   101→            if len(body) != 1:
   102→                continue
   103→            attr = _is_delegation_stmt(body[0])
   104→            if attr:
   105→                delegating_methods.setdefault(attr, []).append(method.name)
   106→
   107→        if not delegating_methods:
   108→            continue
   109→
   110→        # Use the most common delegate target
   111→        top_attr = max(delegating_methods, key=lambda a: len(delegating_methods[a]))
   112→        delegate_count = len(delegating_methods[top_attr])
   113→        ratio = delegate_count / len(methods)
   114→        if ratio > 0.5:
   115→            results.append(
   116→                {
   117→                    "class_name": node.name,
   118→                    "line": node.lineno,
   119→                    "delegation_ratio": round(ratio, 2),
   120→                    "method_count": len(methods),
   121→                    "delegate_count": delegate_count,
   122→                    "delegate_target": top_attr,
   123→                    "sample_methods": delegating_methods[top_attr][:5],
   124→                }
   125→            )
   126→    return results

   128→def _find_facade_modules(tree: ast.Module, *, loc: int) -> dict | None:
   129→    """Detect modules where >70% of public names come from imports."""
   130→    import_names: set[str] = set()
   131→    defined_names: set[str] = set()
   132→
   133→    for node in ast.iter_child_nodes(tree):
   134→        if isinstance(node, ast.Import):
   135→            for alias in node.names:
   136→                name = alias.asname or alias.name.split(".")[-1]
   137→                import_names.add(name)
   138→        elif isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
   139→            for alias in node.names:
   140→                if alias.name == "*":
   141→                    continue
   142→                name = alias.asname or alias.name
   143→                import_names.add(name)
   144→        elif isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   145→            defined_names.add(node.name)
   146→        elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   147→            defined_names.add(node.name)
   148→        elif isinstance(node, ast.Assign):
   149→            for target in node.targets:
   150→                if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and target.id == "__all__":
   151→                    continue
   152→                if isinstance(target, ast.Name):
   153→                    defined_names.add(target.id)
   154→
   155→    # Remove private names
   156→    public_imports = {n for n in import_names if not n.startswith("_")}
   157→    public_defs = {n for n in defined_names if not n.startswith("_")}
   158→
   159→    total_public = len(public_imports | public_defs)
   160→    if total_public < 3:
   161→        return None
   162→
   163→    # Re-exported = imported names that aren't shadowed by a local definition
   164→    re_exported = public_imports - public_defs
   165→    re_export_ratio = len(re_exported) / total_public
   166→
   167→    if re_export_ratio < 0.7 or len(public_defs) > 3:
   168→        return None
   169→
   170→    return {
   171→        "re_export_ratio": round(re_export_ratio, 2),
   172→        "defined_symbols": len(public_defs),
   173→        "re_exported_symbols": len(re_exported),
   174→        "samples": sorted(re_exported)[:5],
   175→        "loc": loc,
   176→    }

   178→def _collect_typed_dict_defs(
   179→    tree: ast.Module, accumulator: dict[str, set[str]]
   180→) -> None:
   181→    """Collect TypedDict class definitions from a single file's AST."""
   182→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   183→        if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   184→            continue
   185→        is_typed_dict = any(
   186→            (isinstance(b, ast.Name) and b.id == "TypedDict")
   187→            or (isinstance(b, ast.Attribute) and b.attr == "TypedDict")
   188→            for b in node.bases
   189→        )
   190→        if not is_typed_dict:
   191→            continue
   192→        fields: set[str] = set()
   193→        for child in node.body:
   194→            if isinstance(child, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(child.target, ast.Name):
   195→                fields.add(child.target.id)
   196→        if fields:
   197→            accumulator[node.name] = fields
   198→
   199→def _find_typed_dict_usage_violations(
   200→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module],
   201→    typed_dicts: dict[str, set[str]],
   202→) -> list[dict]:
   203→    """Find .get()/.setdefault()/.pop() calls on TypedDict-annotated variables.
   204→
   205→    *parsed_trees* maps absolute file paths to pre-parsed ASTs (built during
   206→    the main collection loop to avoid redundant parses).
   207→
   208→    Returns a list of violation dicts with file, typed_dict_name, violation_type,
   209→    line, field (when extractable), and count.
   210→    """
   211→    if not typed_dicts:
   212→        return []
   213→
   214→    violations: list[dict] = []
   215→    for filepath, tree in parsed_trees.items():
   216→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   217→
   218→        # Collect variable names annotated with known TypedDict types
   219→        typed_vars: dict[str, str] = {}  # var_name -> TypedDict name
   220→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   221→            if isinstance(node, ast.AnnAssign) and isinstance(node.target, ast.Name):
   222→                ann = node.annotation
   223→                ann_name = None
   224→                if isinstance(ann, ast.Name):
   225→                    ann_name = ann.id
   226→                elif isinstance(ann, ast.Attribute):
   227→                    ann_name = ann.attr
   228→                if ann_name in typed_dicts:
   229→                    typed_vars[node.target.id] = ann_name
   230→            # Also check function param annotations
   231→            if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   232→                for arg in node.args.args + node.args.kwonlyargs:
   233→                    ann = arg.annotation
   234→                    if ann is None:
   235→                        continue
   236→                    ann_name = None
   237→                    if isinstance(ann, ast.Name):
   238→                        ann_name = ann.id
   239→                    elif isinstance(ann, ast.Attribute):
   240→                        ann_name = ann.attr
   241→                    if ann_name in typed_dicts:
   242→                        typed_vars[arg.arg] = ann_name
   243→
   244→        if not typed_vars:
   245→            continue
   246→
   247→        # Scan for violation calls — collect per (td_name, method, field)
   248→        hits: list[tuple[str, str, str | None, int]] = []
   249→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   250→            if not isinstance(node, ast.Call):
   251→                continue
   252→            func = node.func
   253→            if not isinstance(func, ast.Attribute):
   254→                continue
   255→            if func.attr not in _VIOLATION_METHODS:
   256→                continue
   257→            if not isinstance(func.value, ast.Name) or func.value.id not in typed_vars:
   258→                continue
   259→            td_name = typed_vars[func.value.id]
   260→            # Extract the field name from the first argument if it's a string constant
   261→            field: str | None = None
   262→            if node.args and isinstance(node.args[0], ast.Constant):
   263→                val = node.args[0].value
   264→                if isinstance(val, str):
   265→                    field = val
   266→            hits.append((td_name, func.attr, field, node.lineno))
   267→
   268→        # Group by (td_name, method, field) for compact reporting
   269→        groups: dict[tuple[str, str, str | None], list[int]] = {}
   270→        for td_name, method, field, lineno in hits:
   271→            groups.setdefault((td_name, method, field), []).append(lineno)
   272→
   273→        for (td_name, method, field), lines in groups.items():
   274→            entry: dict = {
   275→                "file": rpath,
   276→                "typed_dict_name": td_name,
   277→                "violation_type": method,
   278→                "line": lines[0],
   279→                "count": len(lines),
   280→            }
   281→            if field is not None:
   282→                entry["field"] = field
   283→            violations.append(entry)
   284→
   285→    return violations
   286→
   287→
   288→# ── dict[str, Any] annotation scanner ─────────────────────
   289→
   290→
   291→def _find_dict_any_annotations(
   292→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module],
   293→    typed_dict_names: set[str],
   294→) -> list[dict]:
   295→    """Find function parameters/returns annotated as ``dict[str, Any]``.
   296→
   297→    Cross-references parameter names against known TypedDict names to suggest
   298→    concrete alternatives when available.
   299→    """
   300→    results: list[dict] = []
   301→    for filepath, tree in parsed_trees.items():
   302→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   303→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   304→            if not isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
   305→                continue
   306→            # Check args
   307→            for arg in node.args.posonlyargs + node.args.args + node.args.kwonlyargs:
   308→                if arg.annotation and _is_dict_str_any(arg.annotation):
   309→                    alt = _guess_alternative(arg.arg, typed_dict_names)
   310→                    results.append({
   311→                        "file": rpath,
   312→                        "function": node.name,
   313→                        "param": arg.arg,
   314→                        "line": arg.lineno,
   315→                        "known_alternative": alt,
   316→                    })
   317→            # Check return annotation
   318→            if node.returns and _is_dict_str_any(node.returns):
   319→                results.append({
   320→                    "file": rpath,
   321→                    "function": node.name,
   322→                    "param": "(return)",
   323→                    "line": node.lineno,
   324→                    "known_alternative": None,
   325→                })
   326→    return results
   327→
   328→
   329→def _is_dict_str_any(ann: ast.expr) -> bool:
   330→    """Check if annotation is ``dict[str, Any]``."""
   331→    if not isinstance(ann, ast.Subscript):
   332→        return False
   333→    if not (isinstance(ann.value, ast.Name) and ann.value.id == "dict"):
   334→        return False
   335→    sl = ann.slice
   336→    if isinstance(sl, ast.Tuple) and len(sl.elts) == 2:
   337→        first, second = sl.elts
   338→        if isinstance(first, ast.Name) and first.id == "str":
   339→            if isinstance(second, ast.Name) and second.id == "Any":
   340→                return True
   341→    return False
   342→
   343→
   344→def _guess_alternative(param_name: str, typed_dict_names: set[str]) -> str | None:
   345→    """Guess a TypedDict alternative by matching param name fragments."""
   346→    if len(param_name) < 4:
   347→        return None
   348→    lower = param_name.lower()
   349→    matches: list[str] = []
   350→    for td_name in sorted(typed_dict_names):
   351→        if td_name.lower() in lower or lower in td_name.lower():
   352→            matches.append(td_name)
   353→    if len(matches) == 1:
   354→        return matches[0]
   355→    return None
   356→
   357→
   358→# ── Enum bypass scanner ───────────────────────────────────
   359→
   360→# Int values too generic to be meaningful enum bypass signals.
   361→_GENERIC_INT_VALUES: frozenset[object] = frozenset({0, 1, 2, 3, -1, True, False})
   362→
   363→
   364→def _collect_enum_defs(
   365→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module],
   366→) -> dict[tuple[str, str], dict]:
   367→    """Find StrEnum/IntEnum/Enum class defs.
   368→
   369→    Returns ``{(file, name): {file, members: {name: value}}}``.
   370→    Keyed by ``(file, class_name)`` to avoid silently overwriting
   371→    same-named enums from different files.
   372→    """
   373→    _ENUM_BASES = {"StrEnum", "IntEnum", "Enum"}
   374→    result: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
   375→    for filepath, tree in parsed_trees.items():
   376→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   377→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   378→            if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   379→                continue
   380→            is_enum = any(
   381→                (isinstance(b, ast.Name) and b.id in _ENUM_BASES)
   382→                or (isinstance(b, ast.Attribute) and b.attr in _ENUM_BASES)
   383→                for b in node.bases
   384→            )
   385→            if not is_enum:
   386→                continue
   387→            members: dict[str, object] = {}
   388→            for child in node.body:
   389→                if isinstance(child, ast.Assign):
   390→                    for target in child.targets:
   391→                        if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and isinstance(
   392→                            child.value, ast.Constant
   393→                        ):
   394→                            members[target.id] = child.value.value
   395→            if members:
   396→                result[(rpath, node.name)] = {"file": rpath, "members": members}
   397→    return result
   398→
   399→
   400→def _find_enum_bypass(
   401→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module],
   402→    enum_defs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict],
   403→) -> list[dict]:
   404→    """Find raw string/int comparisons that match enum member values.
   405→
   406→    Only flags ``==`` and ``!=`` comparisons (not ``>``, ``<``, etc.).
   407→    Skips generic int literals (0, 1, 2, 3, -1, True, False) since they
   408→    produce too many false positives.  Skips the file where the enum is
   409→    defined (internal comparisons are expected).
   410→    """
   411→    if not enum_defs:
   412→        return []
   413→
   414→    # Collect the set of files that define enums so we can skip them.
   415→    enum_def_files: set[str] = {info["file"] for info in enum_defs.values()}
   416→
   417→    # Build reverse lookup: value → list of (enum_name, member_name).
   418→    # Using a list avoids last-write-wins when two enums share a value.
   419→    value_to_enums: dict[object, list[tuple[str, str]]] = {}
   420→    for (_file, enum_name), info in enum_defs.items():
   421→        for member_name, value in info["members"].items():
   422→            if isinstance(value, str):
   423→                value_to_enums.setdefault(value, []).append((enum_name, member_name))
   424→            elif isinstance(value, int) and value not in _GENERIC_INT_VALUES:
   425→                value_to_enums.setdefault(value, []).append((enum_name, member_name))
   426→
   427→    if not value_to_enums:
   428→        return []
   429→
   430→    results: list[dict] = []
   431→    for filepath, tree in parsed_trees.items():
   432→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   433→        # Skip files that define enums — internal comparisons are expected.
   434→        if rpath in enum_def_files:
   435→            continue
   436→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   437→            if not isinstance(node, ast.Compare):
   438→                continue
   439→            # Only flag == and != operators.
   440→            if not all(isinstance(op, (ast.Eq, ast.NotEq)) for op in node.ops):
   441→                continue
   442→            # Check all comparators (left + comparators)
   443→            for const_node in [node.left, *node.comparators]:
   444→                if not isinstance(const_node, ast.Constant):
   445→                    continue
   446→                [REDACTED]
   447→                if key in value_to_enums:
   448→                    for enum_name, member in value_to_enums[key]:
   449→                        results.append({
   450→                            "file": rpath,
   451→                            "line": node.lineno,
   452→                            "enum_name": enum_name,
   453→                            "member": member,
   454→                            "raw_value": repr(key),
   455→                        })
   456→    return results
   457→
   458→
   459→# ── Type strategy census ──────────────────────────────────
   460→
   461→
   462→def _census_type_strategies(
   463→    parsed_trees: dict[str, ast.Module],
   464→) -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
   465→    """Count domain object definitions by strategy.
   466→
   467→    Returns ``{strategy: [{name, file, field_count}]}``.
   468→    """
   469→    strategies: dict[str, list[dict]] = {
   470→        "TypedDict": [],
   471→        "dataclass": [],
   472→        "frozen_dataclass": [],
   473→        "NamedTuple": [],
   474→    }
   475→    for filepath, tree in parsed_trees.items():
   476→        rpath = rel(filepath)
   477→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   478→            if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
   479→                continue
   480→            field_count = sum(
   481→                1 for c in node.body if isinstance(c, ast.AnnAssign)
   482→            )
   483→            entry = {"name": node.name, "file": rpath, "field_count": field_count}
   484→
   485→            # TypedDict
   486→            if any(
   487→                (isinstance(b, ast.Name) and b.id == "TypedDict")
   488→                or (isinstance(b, ast.Attribute) and b.attr == "TypedDict")
   489→                for b in node.bases
   490→            ):
   491→                strategies["TypedDict"].append(entry)
   492→                continue
   493→
   494→            # NamedTuple
   495→            if any(
   496→                (isinstance(b, ast.Name) and b.id == "NamedTuple")
   497→                or (isinstance(b, ast.Attribute) and b.attr == "NamedTuple")
   498→                for b in node.bases
   499→            ):
   500→                strategies["NamedTuple"].append(entry)
   501→                continue
   502→
   503→            # dataclass (check decorators)
   504→            for dec in node.decorator_list:
   505→                is_dc = False
   506→                is_frozen = False
   507→                if isinstance(dec, ast.Name) and dec.id == "dataclass":
   508→                    is_dc = True
   509→                elif isinstance(dec, ast.Attribute) and dec.attr == "dataclass":
   510→                    is_dc = True
   511→                elif isinstance(dec, ast.Call):
   512→                    func = dec.func
   513→                    if (isinstance(func, ast.Name) and func.id == "dataclass") or (
   514→                        isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr == "dataclass"
   515→                    ):
   516→                        is_dc = True
   517→                        # Check for frozen=True
   518→                        for kw in dec.keywords:
   519→                            if (
   520→                                kw.arg == "frozen"
   521→                                and isinstance(kw.value, ast.Constant)
   522→                                and kw.value.value is True
   523→                            ):
   524→                                is_frozen = True
   525→                if is_dc:
   526→                    [REDACTED] if is_frozen else "dataclass"
   527→                    strategies[key].append(entry)
   528→                    break
   529→
   530→    # Remove empty strategies
   531→    return {k: v for k, v in strategies.items() if v}
   532→
   533→
   534→__all__ = [
   535→    "_census_type_strategies",
   536→    "_collect_enum_defs",
   537→    "_collect_typed_dict_defs",
   538→    "_find_delegation_heavy_classes",
   539→    "_find_dict_any_annotations",
   540→    "_find_enum_bypass",
   541→    "_find_facade_modules",
   542→    "_find_python_passthrough_wrappers",
   543→    "_find_typed_dict_usage_violations",
   544→    "_is_delegation_stmt",
   545→    "_python_passthrough_target",
   546→]
```

```
1→"""Shared helpers for language-specific re-export facade detectors."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from collections.abc import Callable
     6→
     7→DEFAULT_MAX_IMPORTERS = 20
     8→
     9→
    10→def _facade_tier_confidence(importer_count: int) -> tuple[int, str]:
    11→    """Determine tier and confidence for a facade based on importer count.
    12→
    13→    ≤5 importers: tier 2, confidence high   (easy removal)
    14→    6-20 importers: tier 3, confidence medium (moderate effort)
    15→    >20 importers: tier 4, confidence medium  (large-scale refactor)
    16→    """
    17→    if importer_count <= 5:
    18→        return 2, "high"
    19→    if importer_count <= 20:
    20→        return 3, "medium"
    21→    return 4, "medium"
    22→
    23→
    24→def detect_reexport_facades_common(
    25→    graph: dict,
    26→    *,
    27→    is_facade_fn: Callable[[str], dict | None],
    28→    max_importers: int = DEFAULT_MAX_IMPORTERS,
    29→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    30→    """Collect file-level re-export facades using a language detector callback.
    31→
    32→    By default this excludes very high-importer facades (importers > 20),
    33→    but callers can override the ceiling for broader scans.
    34→    """
    35→    entries: list[dict] = []
    36→    total_checked = 0
    37→
    38→    for filepath, node in graph.items():
    39→        total_checked += 1
    40→
    41→        result = is_facade_fn(filepath)
    42→        if not result:
    43→            continue
    44→
    45→        importer_count = node.get("importer_count", 0)
    46→        if importer_count > max_importers:
    47→            continue
    48→
    49→        tier, confidence = _facade_tier_confidence(importer_count)
    50→
    51→        entries.append(
    52→            {
    53→                "file": filepath,
    54→                "loc": result["loc"],
    55→                "importers": importer_count,
    56→                "imports_from": result["imports_from"],
    57→                "kind": "file",
    58→                "tier": tier,
    59→                "confidence": confidence,
    60→            }
    61→        )
    62→
    63→    return entries, total_checked
    64→
    65→
    66→__all__ = [
    67→    "DEFAULT_MAX_IMPORTERS",
    68→    "_facade_tier_confidence",
    69→    "detect_reexport_facades_common",
    70→]
    71→
```
