   125→            override_existing or "display_name" not in payload
   126→        ):
   127→            payload["display_name"] = prompt_meta["display_name"]
   128→        if "weight" in prompt_meta and (override_existing or "weight" not in payload):
   129→            payload["weight"] = prompt_meta["weight"]
   130→        if "reset_on_scan" in prompt_meta and (
   131→            override_existing or "reset_on_scan" not in payload
   132→        ):
   133→            payload["reset_on_scan"] = prompt_meta["reset_on_scan"]
   134→
   135→        if dim in defaults:
   136→            payload["enabled_by_default"] = True
   137→        if "enabled_by_default" in prompt_meta:
   138→            if override_existing:
   139→                payload["enabled_by_default"] = bool(prompt_meta["enabled_by_default"])
   140→            else:
   141→                payload["enabled_by_default"] = bool(
   142→                    payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)
   143→                    or prompt_meta["enabled_by_default"]
   144→                )
   145→
   146→
   147→def _available_languages() -> list[str]:
   148→    try:
   149→        return list(available_langs())
   150→    except (ImportError, ValueError, TypeError, RuntimeError):
   151→        return []
   152→
   153→
   154→def _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(
   155→    *,
   156→    lang_name: str | None,
   157→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   158→    """Build merged metadata for subjective dimensions."""
   159→    out: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
   160→
   161→    shared_defaults, shared_prompts, _ = load_dimensions()
   162→    _merge_dimension_meta(out, dimensions=shared_defaults, prompts=shared_prompts)
   163→
   164→    langs = [lang_name] if isinstance(lang_name, str) and lang_name.strip() else _available_languages()
   165→    for name in langs:
   166→        try:
   167→            lang_defaults, lang_prompts, _ = load_dimensions_for_lang(name)
   168→            _merge_dimension_meta(
   169→                out,
   170→                dimensions=lang_defaults,
   171→                prompts=lang_prompts,
   172→                override_existing=bool(lang_name),
   173→            )
   174→        except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
   175→            logger.debug("Failed to load dimensions for lang %s: %s", name, exc)
   176→            continue
   177→
   178→    for dim, payload in out.items():
   179→        payload.setdefault(
   180→            "display_name",
   181→            _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.get(dim, _title_display_name(dim)),
   182→        )
   183→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   184→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   185→        if dim in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES:
   186→            payload.setdefault(
   187→                "reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS
   188→            )
   189→        else:
   190→            payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   191→
   192→    # Preserve legacy dimensions even if a payload temporarily drops one.
   193→    for dim, display in _LEGACY_DISPLAY_NAMES.items():
   194→        payload = out.setdefault(dim, {})
   195→        payload.setdefault("display_name", display)
   196→        payload.setdefault("weight", _LEGACY_WEIGHT_BY_DIMENSION.get(dim, 1.0))
   197→        payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", True)
   198→        payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", dim in _LEGACY_RESET_ON_SCAN_DIMENSIONS)
   199→
   200→    return out
   201→
   202→
   203→@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
   204→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata() -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   205→    """Return merged metadata across all known dimensions/languages."""
   206→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=None)
   207→
   208→
   209→@lru_cache(maxsize=16)
   210→def load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(
   211→    lang_name: str | None,
   212→) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   213→    """Return merged metadata for one language (with language overrides)."""
   214→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   215→    return _build_subjective_dimension_metadata(lang_name=normalized)
   216→
   217→
   218→def _metadata_registry(lang_name: str | None) -> dict[str, dict[str, object]]:
   219→    normalized = _normalize_lang_name(lang_name)
   220→    if normalized is None:
   221→        return load_subjective_dimension_metadata()
   222→    return load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang(normalized)
   223→
   224→
   225→def _dimension_metadata_payload(
   226→    dimension_name: str,
   227→    *,
   228→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   229→) -> dict[str, object]:
   230→    dim = _normalize_dimension_name(dimension_name)
   231→    all_meta = _metadata_registry(lang_name)
   232→    payload = dict(all_meta.get(dim, {}))
   233→
   234→    payload.setdefault("display_name", _title_display_name(dim))
   235→    payload.setdefault("weight", 1.0)
   236→    payload.setdefault("enabled_by_default", False)
   237→    payload.setdefault("reset_on_scan", True)
   238→    return payload
   239→
   240→
   241→def get_dimension_metadata(
   242→    dimension_name: str,
   243→    *,
   244→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   245→) -> dict[str, object]:
   246→    """Return metadata for one dimension key (with sane defaults)."""
   247→    return _dimension_metadata_payload(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   248→
   249→
   250→def dimension_display_name(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> str:
   251→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   252→    return str(meta.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dimension_name)))
   253→
   254→
   255→def dimension_weight(dimension_name: str, *, lang_name: str | None = None) -> float:
   256→    meta = get_dimension_metadata(dimension_name, lang_name=lang_name)
   257→    raw = meta.get("weight", 1.0)
   258→    if is_numeric(raw):
   259→        return max(0.0, float(raw))
   260→    return 1.0
   261→
   262→
   263→def default_display_names_map(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
   264→    """Display-name map for default subjective dimensions."""
   265→    out: dict[str, str] = {}
   266→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   267→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   268→            continue
   269→        out[dim] = str(payload.get("display_name", _title_display_name(dim)))
   270→    return out
   271→
   272→
   273→def _resettable_default_dimensions_payload(
   274→    *,
   275→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   276→) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   277→    out = []
   278→    for dim, payload in _metadata_registry(lang_name).items():
   279→        if not bool(payload.get("enabled_by_default", False)):
   280→            continue
   281→        if not bool(payload.get("reset_on_scan", True)):
   282→            continue
   283→        out.append(dim)
   284→    return tuple(sorted(set(out)))
   285→
   286→
   287→def resettable_default_dimensions(*, lang_name: str | None = None) -> tuple[str, ...]:
   288→    """Default subjective dimensions that should be reset by scan reset."""
   289→    return _resettable_default_dimensions_payload(lang_name=lang_name)
   290→
   291→
   292→__all__ = [
   293→    "default_display_names_map",
   294→    "dimension_display_name",
   295→    "dimension_weight",
   296→    "extract_prompt_meta",
   297→    "get_dimension_metadata",
   298→    "load_subjective_dimension_metadata",
   299→    "load_subjective_dimension_metadata_for_lang",
   300→    "resettable_default_dimensions",
   301→]
   302→

1→"""Detect module-level mutable state modified from functions within the same module."""

     3→from __future__ import annotations

     5→import ast
     6→import logging

    15→
    16→# Mutable initializer values
    17→_MUTABLE_INIT = (ast.List, ast.Dict, ast.Set)
    18→_MUTABLE_CALL_NAMES = {"set", "list", "dict", "defaultdict", "OrderedDict", "Counter"}
    19→
    20→# Mutating method names
    21→_MUTATING_METHODS = {
    22→    "append",
    23→    "extend",
    24→    "insert",
    25→    "pop",
    26→    "remove",
    27→    "clear",
    28→    "update",
    29→    "setdefault",

    31→    "discard",

    34→
    35→def _is_mutable_init(value: ast.AST) -> bool:
    36→    """Check if an AST value is a mutable initializer ([], {}, set(), etc.)."""
    37→    if isinstance(value, _MUTABLE_INIT):
    38→        return True
    39→    if isinstance(value, ast.Call):
    40→        func = value.func
    41→        if isinstance(func, ast.Name) and func.id in _MUTABLE_CALL_NAMES:
    42→            return True
    43→        if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and func.attr in _MUTABLE_CALL_NAMES:
    44→            return True
    45→    if isinstance(value, ast.Constant) and value.value is None:
    46→        return True
    47→    return False
    48→
    49→
    50→def _is_upper_case(name: str) -> bool:
    51→    """Check if a name is UPPER_CASE (constant convention)."""
    52→    return bool(re.match(r"^_?[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+$", name))
    53→
    54→
    55→
    56→def _collect_module_level_mutables(tree: ast.Module) -> dict[str, int]:
    57→    """Collect module-level names initialized to mutable values.
    58→
    59→    UPPER_CASE names with truly immutable values (strings, ints, tuples,
    60→    frozensets) are already filtered out by ``_is_mutable_init()``.
    61→    UPPER_CASE mutable containers (``REGISTRY = {}``, ``ITEMS = []``) are
    62→    included — they represent runtime-mutated registries, not constants.
    63→    """
    64→    mutables: dict[str, int] = {}
    65→    for stmt in tree.body:
    66→        if isinstance(stmt, ast.Assign):
    67→            for target in stmt.targets:
    68→                if isinstance(target, ast.Name) and _is_mutable_init(stmt.value):
    69→                    if _is_upper_case(target.id) and isinstance(stmt.value, ast.Constant):
    70→                        continue
    71→                    mutables[target.id] = stmt.lineno
    72→        elif (
    73→            isinstance(stmt, ast.AnnAssign)
    74→            and stmt.target
    75→            and isinstance(stmt.target, ast.Name)
    76→        ):
    77→            name = stmt.target.id
    78→            # Mutable initializer → always include regardless of case.
    79→            if stmt.value is not None and _is_mutable_init(stmt.value):
    80→                if _is_upper_case(name) and isinstance(stmt.value, ast.Constant):
    81→                    continue
    82→                mutables[name] = stmt.lineno
    83→            elif _is_optional_annotation(stmt.annotation):
    84→                # Optional without mutable init — exempt UPPER_CASE
    85→                # (likely a sentinel, not a mutable registry).
    86→                if not _is_upper_case(name):
    87→                    mutables[name] = stmt.lineno
    88→    return mutables

    90→
    91→def _is_optional_annotation(ann: ast.AST) -> bool:
    92→    """Check if an annotation looks like Optional[...]."""
    93→    is_optional_subscript = isinstance(ann, ast.Subscript) and (
    94→        (isinstance(ann.value, ast.Name) and ann.value.id == "Optional")
    95→        or (isinstance(ann.value, ast.Attribute) and ann.value.attr == "Optional")
    96→    )
    97→    is_optional_union = (
    98→        isinstance(ann, ast.BinOp)
    99→        and isinstance(ann.op, ast.BitOr)
   100→        and (
   101→            (isinstance(ann.right, ast.Constant) and ann.right.value is None)
   102→            or (isinstance(ann.left, ast.Constant) and ann.left.value is None)
   103→        )
   104→    )
   105→    return is_optional_subscript or is_optional_union
   106→
   107→
   108→def _find_mutations_in_functions(
   109→    tree: ast.Module, mutables: dict[str, int]
   110→) -> dict[str, list[int]]:
   111→    """Find functions that reassign or mutate module-level mutable names.
   112→
   113→    Returns {name: [line numbers where mutation occurs]}.
   114→
   115→    Bare assignments (name = x) and augmented assignments (name += x) only count
   116→    as mutations when the function has an explicit `global name` declaration —
   117→    without it, Python creates a local variable. Subscript assignments (name[k] = v)
   118→    and method calls (name.append(x)) don't need `global` because they operate on
   119→    the object reference, not rebind the name.
   120→    """
   121→    mutations: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
   122→
   123→    for node in ast.walk(tree):
   124→        if not isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   125→            continue
   126→        # Skip if name is a parameter
   127→        param_names = {
   128→            a.arg for a in node.args.args + node.args.posonlyargs + node.args.kwonlyargs
   129→        }
   130→        # Collect names declared `global` in this function
   131→        global_names: set[str] = set()
   132→        for child in ast.walk(node):
   133→            if isinstance(child, ast.Global):
   134→                global_names.update(child.names)
   135→
   136→        for child in ast.walk(node):
   137→            if isinstance(child, ast.Assign):
   138→                for target in child.targets:
   139→                    # Bare name assignment: requires `global` to actually mutate
   140→                    if (
   141→                        isinstance(target, ast.Name)
   142→                        and target.id in mutables
   143→                        and target.id not in param_names
   144→                    ):
   145→                        if target.id in global_names:
   146→                            mutations.setdefault(target.id, []).append(child.lineno)
   147→                    # Subscript assignment (name[k] = v): operates on the object, no `global` needed
   148→                    elif isinstance(target, ast.Subscript) and isinstance(
   149→                        target.value, ast.Name
   150→                    ):
   151→                        if (
   152→                            target.value.id in mutables
   153→                            and target.value.id not in param_names
   154→                        ):
   155→                            mutations.setdefault(target.value.id, []).append(
   156→                                child.lineno
   157→                            )
   158→            # Augmented assignment (name += x): requires `global` to actually mutate
   159→            elif isinstance(child, ast.AugAssign):
   160→                if (
   161→                    isinstance(child.target, ast.Name)
   162→                    and child.target.id in mutables
   163→                    and child.target.id not in param_names
   164→                    and child.target.id in global_names
   165→                ):
   166→                    mutations.setdefault(child.target.id, []).append(child.lineno)
   167→            # Mutating method call: name.append(...) — no `global` needed
   168→            elif isinstance(child, ast.Call) and isinstance(child.func, ast.Attribute):
   169→                if (
   170→                    child.func.attr in _MUTATING_METHODS
   171→                    and isinstance(child.func.value, ast.Name)
   172→                    and child.func.value.id in mutables
   173→                    and child.func.value.id not in param_names
   174→                ):
   175→                    mutations.setdefault(child.func.value.id, []).append(child.lineno)
   176→
   177→    return mutations
   178→
   179→
   180→def _detect_in_module(filepath: str, tree: ast.Module, entries: list[dict]):
   181→    """Detect global mutable config patterns in a single module."""
   182→    mutables = _collect_module_level_mutables(tree)
   183→    if not mutables:
   184→        return
   185→
   186→    mutations = _find_mutations_in_functions(tree, mutables)
   187→    if not mutations:
   188→        return
   189→
   190→    for name, mutation_lines in mutations.items():
   191→        defn_line = mutables[name]
   192→        entries.append(
   193→            {
   194→                "file": filepath,
   195→                "name": name,
   196→                "line": defn_line,
   197→                "mutation_lines": mutation_lines[:5],
   198→                "mutation_count": len(mutation_lines),
   199→                "confidence": "medium",
   200→                "summary": (
   201→                    f"Module-level mutable '{name}' (line {defn_line}) "
   202→                    f"modified from {len(mutation_lines)} site(s)"
   203→                ),
   204→            }
   205→        )
   206→
   207→
   208→# ── Import-binding footgun detection ─────────────────────
   209→
   210→
   211→def _detect_stale_imports(
   212→    path: Path,
   213→    mutated_names: dict[str, set[str]],
   214→    entries: list[dict],
   215→):
   216→    """Detect ``from X import mutable_name`` that creates a stale binding.
   217→
   218→    When a module-level mutable is reassigned (via ``global``), other modules
   219→    that import the name directly get a stale copy.  They should import the
   220→    module and access the attribute at call time instead.
   221→    """
   222→    files = find_py_files(path)
   223→
   224→    for filepath in files:
   225→        try:
   226→            p = (
   227→                Path(filepath)
   228→                if Path(filepath).is_absolute()
   229→                else get_project_root() / filepath
   230→            )
   231→            content = p.read_text()
   232→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
   233→            logger.debug(
   234→                "Skipping unreadable python file %s in stale-import pass: %s",
   235→                filepath,
   236→                exc,
   237→            )
   238→            continue
   239→
   240→        try:
   241→            tree = ast.parse(content, filename=filepath)
   242→        except SyntaxError as exc:
   243→            logger.debug(
   244→                "Skipping unparseable python file %s in stale-import pass: %s",
   245→                filepath,
   246→                exc,
   247→            )
   248→            continue
   249→
   250→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   251→            if not isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom):
   252→                continue
   253→            module = node.module or ""
   254→            # Check if any imported name is a mutated global in the source module
   255→            for source_module, names in mutated_names.items():
   256→                # Match by suffix (e.g., "desloppify.utils" matches "from .utils import")
   257→                if not (
   258→                    module == source_module
   259→                    or module.endswith(f".{source_module}")
   260→                    or source_module.endswith(f".{module}")
   261→                ):
   262→                    continue
   263→                for alias in node.names:
   264→                    if alias.name in names:
   265→                        entries.append(
   266→                            {
   267→                                "file": filepath,
   268→                                "name": alias.name,
   269→                                "line": node.lineno,
   270→                                "mutation_lines": [],
   271→                                "mutation_count": 0,
   272→                                "confidence": "high",
   273→                                "summary": (
   274→                                    f"'from {module} import {alias.name}' creates stale binding — "
   275→                                    f"'{alias.name}' is reassigned at runtime. Import the module instead."
   276→                                ),
   277→                            }
   278→                        )
   279→
   280→
   281→def detect_global_mutable_config(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   282→    """Detect module-level mutable state that gets modified from functions.
   283→
   284→    Also detects stale import bindings: other modules that `from X import name`
   285→    a mutable that gets reassigned, which creates a stale copy.
   286→
   287→    Returns (entries, total_files_checked).
   288→    """
   289→    files = find_py_files(path)
   290→    entries: list[dict] = []
   291→
   292→    # Phase 1: collect mutated globals per module
   293→    mutated_names: dict[str, set[str]] = {}  # {module_path: {name, ...}}
   294→
   295→    for filepath in files:
   296→        try:
   297→            p = (
   298→                Path(filepath)
   299→                if Path(filepath).is_absolute()
   300→                else get_project_root() / filepath
   301→            )
   302→            content = p.read_text()
   303→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
   304→            logger.debug(
   305→                "Skipping unreadable python file %s in mutable-state pass: %s",
   306→                filepath,
   307→                exc,
   308→            )
   309→            continue
   310→
   311→        try:
   312→            tree = ast.parse(content, filename=filepath)
   313→        except SyntaxError as exc:
   314→            logger.debug(
   315→                "Skipping unparseable python file %s in mutable-state pass: %s",
   316→                filepath,
   317→                exc,
   318→            )
   319→            continue
   320→
   321→        _detect_in_module(filepath, tree, entries)
   322→
   323→        # Track which modules have reassigned globals (need `global` keyword)
   324→        mutables = _collect_module_level_mutables(tree)
   325→        if mutables:
   326→            # Only track names that are reassigned (not just mutated via methods)
   327→            reassigned = set()
   328→            for node in ast.walk(tree):
   329→                if not isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   330→                    continue
   331→                global_names: set[str] = set()
   332→                for child in ast.walk(node):
   333→                    if isinstance(child, ast.Global):
   334→                        global_names.update(child.names)
   335→                for name in global_names:
   336→                    if name in mutables:
   337→                        reassigned.add(name)
   338→            if reassigned:
   339→                # Convert filepath to dotted module path
   340→                module_path = filepath.replace("/", ".").replace("\\", ".")
   341→                if module_path.endswith(".py"):
   342→                    module_path = module_path[:-3]
   343→                mutated_names[module_path] = reassigned
   344→
   345→    # Phase 2: detect stale import bindings
   346→    if mutated_names:
   347→        _detect_stale_imports(path, mutated_names, entries)
   348→
   349→    return entries, len(files)

1→"""Validation/parsing helpers for review dimensions payloads."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.core.text.text_api import is_numeric
     6→

    11→
    12→def validate_payload_keys(
    13→    payload: dict,
    14→    *,
    15→    required: set[str],
    16→    context: str,
    17→    optional: set[str] | None = None,
    18→) -> None:
    19→    """Validate payload has required keys and no unknown keys."""
    20→    optional_keys = optional or set()
    21→    allowed = set(required) | set(optional_keys)
    22→    actual = set(payload)
    23→    missing = sorted(required - actual)
    24→    extra = sorted(actual - allowed)
    25→    if missing or extra:
    26→        raise ValueError(
    27→            f"{context} keys invalid (missing={missing or []}, extra={extra or []})"
    28→        )

    31→def validate_string_list(value: object, *, context: str) -> list[str]:

    33→    if not isinstance(value, list) or not value:
    34→        raise ValueError(f"{context} must be a non-empty list of strings")

   175→    dims: list[str] = []
   176→    if dims_key in payload:
   177→        dims = validate_dimensions_list(
   178→            payload.get(dims_key),

   181→    prompts = validate_dimension_prompts(

   185→    system_prompt = validate_system_prompt(
   186→        payload.get("system_prompt"),
   187→        context=f"{context_prefix}.system_prompt",
   188→    )
   189→
   190→    for dim_name, entry in prompts.items():
   191→        meta = entry.get("meta")
   192→        if isinstance(meta, dict) and meta.get("enabled_by_default") is True:
   193→            if dim_name not in dims:
   194→                dims.append(dim_name)
   195→
   196→    if not dims:
   197→        raise ValueError(
   198→            f"{context_prefix} must define at least one default dimension "
   199→            "(either via default_dimensions or dimension_prompts.*.meta.enabled_by_default)"
   200→        )
   201→
   202→    missing = [dim for dim in dims if dim not in prompts]
   203→    if missing:
   204→        raise ValueError(
   205→            f"{context_prefix}.{dims_key} missing prompts: {sorted(missing)}"
   206→        )
   207→
   208→    return dims, prompts, system_prompt

1→"""Dict key flow analysis — detect dead writes, phantom reads, typos, and schema drift."""

     3→from __future__ import annotations

     5→import ast

     7→import logging

    19→
    20→@dataclass
    21→class TrackedDict:
    22→    """A dict variable tracked within a single scope."""

    24→    name: str
    25→    created_line: int
    26→    locally_created: bool
    27→    returned_or_passed: bool = False

    31→    reads: dict[str, list[int]] = field(default_factory=lambda: defaultdict(list))
    32→    bulk_read: bool = False  # .keys(), .values(), .items(), for x in d
    33→
    34→
    35→# Variable name patterns that suppress dead-write warnings
    36→_CONFIG_NAMES = {
    37→    "config",
    38→    "settings",
    39→    "defaults",
    40→    "options",
    41→    "kwargs",
    42→    "context",
    43→    "ctx",
    44→    "env",
    45→    "params",
    46→    "metadata",
    47→    "headers",
    48→    "attrs",
    49→    "attributes",
    50→    "props",
    51→    "properties",
    52→}
    53→
    54→# Dict method → effect
    55→_READ_METHODS = {"get", "pop", "setdefault", "__getitem__", "__contains__"}
    56→_WRITE_METHODS = {"update", "setdefault", "__setitem__"}
    57→_BULK_READ_METHODS = {"keys", "values", "items", "copy", "__iter__"}
    58→
    59→
    60→def _levenshtein(s1: str, s2: str) -> int:
    61→    """Compute Levenshtein edit distance between two strings."""
    62→    if len(s1) < len(s2):
    63→        return _levenshtein(s2, s1)
    64→    if len(s2) == 0:
    65→        return len(s1)
    66→    prev = list(range(len(s2) + 1))
    67→    for i, c1 in enumerate(s1):
    68→        curr = [i + 1]
    69→        for j, c2 in enumerate(s2):
    70→            cost = 0 if c1 == c2 else 1
    71→            curr.append(min(curr[j] + 1, prev[j + 1] + 1, prev[j] + cost))
    72→        prev = curr
    73→    return prev[-1]
    74→
    75→
    76→def _is_singular_plural(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    77→    """Check if a and b are singular/plural variants of each other."""
    78→    return (
    79→        a + "s" == b
    80→        or b + "s" == a
    81→        or a + "es" == b
    82→        or b + "es" == a
    83→        or (a.endswith("ies") and a[:-3] + "y" == b)
    84→        or (b.endswith("ies") and b[:-3] + "y" == a)
    85→    )
    86→
    87→
    88→# ── AST Visitor ───────────────────────────────────────────
    89→
    90→
    91→def _load_dict_key_visitor():
    92→    module = importlib.import_module(".visitor", package=__package__)
    93→    return module.DictKeyVisitor
    94→
    95→
    96→def _get_name(node: ast.expr) -> str | None:
    97→    """Extract variable name from a Name or Attribute(self.x) node."""
    98→    if isinstance(node, ast.Name):
    99→        return node.id
   100→    return (
   101→        f"{node.value.id}.{node.attr}"
   102→        if isinstance(node, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(node.value, ast.Name)
   103→        else None
   104→    )

   110→        return node.value
   111→    return None

   114→# ── Pass 1: Single-scope dict key analysis ────────────────
   115→
   116→
   117→def detect_dict_key_flow(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   118→    """Walk all .py files, run DictKeyVisitor. Returns (entries, files_checked)."""
   119→    dict_key_visitor = _load_dict_key_visitor()
   120→    files = find_py_files(path)
   121→    all_issues: list[dict] = []
   122→    all_literals: list[dict] = []
   123→
   124→    for filepath in files:
   125→        try:
   126→            p = (
   127→                Path(filepath)
   128→                if Path(filepath).is_absolute()
   129→                else get_project_root() / filepath
   130→            )
   131→            source = p.read_text()
   132→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
   133→            logger.debug(
   134→                "Skipping unreadable python file %s in dict-key pass: %s", filepath, exc
   135→            )
   136→            continue
   137→
   138→        try:
   139→            tree = ast.parse(source, filename=filepath)
   140→        except SyntaxError as exc:
   141→            logger.debug(
   142→                "Skipping unparseable python file %s in dict-key pass: %s",
   143→                filepath,
   144→                exc,
   145→            )
   146→            continue
   147→
   148→        visitor = dict_key_visitor(filepath)
   149→        visitor.visit(tree)
   150→        all_issues.extend(visitor._issues)
   151→        all_literals.extend(visitor._dict_literals)
   152→
   153→    return all_issues, len(files)
   154→
   155→
   156→# ── Pass 2: Schema drift clustering ──────────────────────
   157→
   158→
   159→def _jaccard(a: frozenset, b: frozenset) -> float:
   160→    if not a and not b:
   161→        return 1.0
   162→    return len(a & b) / len(a | b)
   163→
   164→
   165→def _read_python_file(filepath: str, *, path: Path) -> str | None:
   166→    try:
   167→        file_path = (
   168→            Path(filepath) if Path(filepath).is_absolute() else get_project_root() / filepath
   169→        )
   170→        return file_path.read_text()
   171→    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
   172→        logger.debug(
   173→            "Skipping unreadable python file %s in schema-drift pass: %s", filepath, exc
   174→        )
   175→        return None
   176→
   177→
   178→def _parse_python_ast(source: str, *, filepath: str) -> ast.AST | None:
   179→    try:
   180→        return ast.parse(source, filename=filepath)
   181→    except SyntaxError as exc:
   182→        logger.debug(
   183→            "Skipping unparseable python file %s in schema-drift pass: %s",
   184→            filepath,
   185→            exc,
   186→        )
   187→        return None
   188→
   189→
   190→def _extract_literal_keyset(node: ast.Dict) -> frozenset[str] | None:
   191→    if len(node.keys) < 3:
   192→        return None
   193→    if any(key is None for key in node.keys):
   194→        return None  # Has **spread
   195→    literal_keys: list[str] = []
   196→    for key in node.keys:
   197→        if key is None:
   198→            continue
   199→        if not isinstance(key, ast.Constant) or not isinstance(key.value, str):
   200→            return None
   201→        literal_keys.append(key.value)
   202→    return frozenset(literal_keys)
   203→
   204→
   205→def _collect_schema_literals(path: Path, files: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
   206→    literals: list[dict] = []
   207→    for filepath in files:
   208→        source = _read_python_file(filepath, path=path)
   209→        if source is None:
   210→            continue
   211→        tree = _parse_python_ast(source, filepath=filepath)
   212→        if tree is None:
   213→            continue
   214→
   215→        for node in ast.walk(tree):
   216→            if not isinstance(node, ast.Dict):
   217→                continue
   218→            keyset = _extract_literal_keyset(node)
   219→            if keyset is None:
   220→                continue
   221→            literals.append({"file": filepath, "line": node.lineno, "keys": keyset})
   222→    return literals
   223→
   224→
   225→def _cluster_by_jaccard(
   226→    literals: list[dict], *, threshold: float = 0.8
   227→) -> list[list[dict]]:
   228→    """Greedy single-linkage clustering by Jaccard similarity threshold."""
   229→    clusters: list[list[dict]] = []
   230→    assigned = [False] * len(literals)
   231→
   232→    for index, literal in enumerate(literals):
   233→        if assigned[index]:
   234→            continue
   235→        cluster = [literal]
   236→        assigned[index] = True
   237→        for probe_idx in range(index + 1, len(literals)):
   238→            if assigned[probe_idx]:
   239→                continue
   240→            candidate = literals[probe_idx]
   241→            if any(
   242→                _jaccard(member["keys"], candidate["keys"]) >= threshold
   243→                for member in cluster
   244→            ):
   245→                cluster.append(candidate)
   246→                assigned[probe_idx] = True
   247→        clusters.append(cluster)
   248→
   249→    return clusters
   250→
   251→
   252→def _cluster_key_frequency(cluster: list[dict]) -> dict[str, int]:
   253→    freq: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
   254→    for member in cluster:
   255→        for key in member["keys"]:
   256→            freq[key] += 1
   257→    return freq
   258→
   259→
   260→def _closest_consensus_key(outlier_key: str, consensus: set[str]) -> str | None:
   261→    for consensus_key in consensus:
   262→        distance = _levenshtein(outlier_key, consensus_key)
   263→        if distance <= 2 or _is_singular_plural(outlier_key, consensus_key):
   264→            return consensus_key
   265→    return None
   266→
   267→
   268→def _build_schema_drift_issues(clusters: list[list[dict]]) -> list[dict]:
   269→    issues: list[dict] = []
   270→    for cluster in clusters:
   271→        if len(cluster) < 3:
   272→            continue
   273→
   274→        key_freq = _cluster_key_frequency(cluster)
   275→        threshold = 0.3 * len(cluster)
   276→        consensus = {key for key, count in key_freq.items() if count >= threshold}
   277→
   278→        for member in cluster:
   279→            outlier_keys = member["keys"] - consensus
   280→            for outlier_key in outlier_keys:
   281→                close_match = _closest_consensus_key(outlier_key, consensus)
   282→                present = key_freq[outlier_key]
   283→                tier = 2 if len(cluster) >= 5 else 3
   284→                confidence = "high" if len(cluster) >= 5 else "medium"
   285→                suggestion = f' Did you mean "{close_match}"?' if close_match else ""
   286→                issues.append(
   287→                    {
   288→                        "file": member["file"],
   289→                        "kind": "schema_drift",
   290→                        "key": outlier_key,
   291→                        "line": member["line"],
   292→                        "tier": tier,
   293→                        "confidence": confidence,
   294→                        "summary": (
   295→                            f"Schema drift: {len(cluster) - present}/{len(cluster)} dict literals use different "
   296→                            f'key, but {member["file"]}:{member["line"]} uses "{outlier_key}".{suggestion}'
   297→                        ),
   298→                        "detail": (
   299→                            f'Cluster of {len(cluster)} similar dict literals. Key "{outlier_key}" appears in '
   300→                            f"only {present}. Consensus keys: {sorted(consensus)}"
   301→                        ),
   302→                    }
   303→                )
   304→    return issues
   305→
   306→
   307→def detect_schema_drift(path: Path) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
   308→    """Cluster dict literals by key similarity, report outlier keys.
   309→
   310→    Returns (entries, literals_checked).
   311→    """
   312→    files = find_py_files(path)
   313→    all_literals = _collect_schema_literals(path, files)
   314→
   315→    if len(all_literals) < 3:
   316→        return [], len(all_literals)
   317→
   318→    clusters = _cluster_by_jaccard(all_literals, threshold=0.8)
   319→    issues = _build_schema_drift_issues(clusters)
   320→
   321→    return issues, len(all_literals)
   322→

   325→    "TrackedDict",
   326→    "detect_dict_key_flow",
   327→    "detect_schema_drift",
   328→]

    18→def _mark_returned_or_passed(visitor: DictKeyVisitor, node: ast.expr) -> None:
    19→    """Mark a tracked dict expression as escaped via return/call boundary."""
    20→    if isinstance(node, ast.Tuple):
    21→        for elt in node.elts:
    22→            _mark_returned_or_passed(visitor, elt)
    23→        return
    24→    if isinstance(node, ast.List | ast.Set):
    25→        for elt in node.elts:
    26→            _mark_returned_or_passed(visitor, elt)
    27→        return
    28→    if isinstance(node, ast.Dict):
    29→        for key in node.keys:
    30→            if key is not None:
    31→                _mark_returned_or_passed(visitor, key)
    32→        for value in node.values:
    33→            _mark_returned_or_passed(visitor, value)
    34→        return
    35→    name = _get_name(node)
    36→    if not name:
    37→        return
    38→    tracked = visitor._get_tracked(name)
    39→    if tracked:
    40→        tracked.returned_or_passed = True
    41→

    43→def _mark_assignment_escape(
    44→    visitor: DictKeyVisitor,
    45→    targets: list[ast.expr],
    46→    value: ast.expr,
    47→) -> None:
    48→    """Mark tracked dict as escaped when assigned into container/attribute slots."""
    49→    name = _get_name(value)
    50→    if not name:
    51→        return
    52→    tracked = visitor._get_tracked(name)
    53→    if tracked is None:
    54→        return
    55→    for target in targets:
    56→        if isinstance(target, ast.Subscript | ast.Attribute):
    57→            tracked.returned_or_passed = True

    62→    """Update tracked dict read/write metadata from a call expression."""
    63→    if isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute):

    67→            tracked = visitor._get_tracked(name)

    69→                if method in ("get", "pop", "__getitem__", "__contains__"):
    70→                    if node.args:
    71→                        key = _get_str_key(node.args[0])

    74→                        else:

    76→                elif method == "setdefault":

    78→                        key = _get_str_key(node.args[0])

    98→                    tracked.bulk_read = True

   113→def _analyze_scope_issues(
   114→    visitor: DictKeyVisitor,
   115→    scope: dict[str, TrackedDict],
   116→    func_name: str,
   117→    *,
   118→    is_class: bool = False,
   119→) -> list[dict]:
   120→    """Analyze a completed scope and return dict-key issues."""
   121→    issues: list[dict] = []
   122→    for tracked in scope.values():
   123→        if not tracked.locally_created:
   124→            continue
   125→
   126→        suppress_dead = (
   127→            tracked.returned_or_passed
   128→            or tracked.has_dynamic_key
   129→            or tracked.has_star_unpack
   130→            or tracked.bulk_read
   131→            or any(
   132→                tracked.name.lower().endswith(name) or tracked.name.lower() == name
   133→                for name in _CONFIG_NAMES
   134→            )
   135→            or (not is_class and func_name in ("__init__", "setUp", "setup"))
   136→            or sum(len(lines) for lines in tracked.writes.values()) < 3
   137→        )
   138→
   139→        written_keys = set(tracked.writes.keys())
   140→        read_keys = set(tracked.reads.keys())
   141→
   142→        dead_keys = written_keys - read_keys
   143→        if not suppress_dead:
   144→            for key in sorted(dead_keys):
   145→                line = tracked.writes[key][0]
   146→                issues.append(
   147→                    {
   148→                        "file": visitor.filepath,
   149→                        "kind": "dead_write",
   150→                        "variable": tracked.name,
   151→                        "key": key,
   152→                        "line": line,
   153→                        "func": func_name,
   154→                        "tier": 3,
   155→                        "confidence": "medium",
   156→                        "summary": (
   157→                            f'Dict key "{key}" written to `{tracked.name}` '
   158→                            f"at line {line} but never read"
   159→                        ),
   160→                        "detail": f"in {func_name}()",
   161→                    }
   162→                )
   163→
   164→        phantom_keys = read_keys - written_keys
   165→        for key in sorted(phantom_keys):
   166→            line = tracked.reads[key][0]
   167→            issues.append(
   168→                {
   169→                    "file": visitor.filepath,
   170→                    "kind": "phantom_read",
   171→                    "variable": tracked.name,
   172→                    "key": key,
   173→                    "line": line,
   174→                    "func": func_name,
   175→                    "tier": 2,
   176→                    "confidence": "high",
   177→                    "summary": (
   178→                        f'Dict key "{key}" read at line {line} '
   179→                        f"but never written to `{tracked.name}`"
   180→                    ),
   181→                    "detail": (
   182→                        f"Created at line {tracked.created_line} in "
   183→                        f"{func_name}() — will raise KeyError or "
   184→                        f"return None via .get()"
   185→                    ),
   186→                }
   187→            )
   188→
   189→        for dead_key in sorted(dead_keys):
   190→            for phantom_key in sorted(phantom_keys):
   191→                distance = _levenshtein(dead_key, phantom_key)
   192→                is_plural_miss = _is_singular_plural(dead_key, phantom_key)
   193→                if distance <= 2 or is_plural_miss:
   194→                    write_line = tracked.writes[dead_key][0]
   195→                    read_line = tracked.reads[phantom_key][0]
   196→                    issues.append(
   197→                        {
   198→                            "file": visitor.filepath,
   199→                            "kind": "near_miss",
   200→                            "variable": tracked.name,
   201→                            "key": f"{dead_key}~{phantom_key}",
   202→                            "line": write_line,
   203→                            "func": func_name,
   204→                            "tier": 2,
   205→                            "confidence": "high",
   206→                            "summary": (
   207→                                f'Possible key typo: "{dead_key}" vs "{phantom_key}" '
   208→                                f"on dict `{tracked.name}` in {func_name}()"
   209→                            ),
   210→                            "detail": (
   211→                                f'Written: "{dead_key}" at line {write_line}, '
   212→                                f'Read: "{phantom_key}" at line {read_line} '
   213→                                f"— edit distance {distance}"
   214→                            ),
   215→                        }
   216→                    )
   217→
   218→        for key, write_lines in tracked.writes.items():
   219→            if len(write_lines) < 2:
   220→                continue
   221→            read_lines = tracked.reads.get(key, [])
   222→            for idx in range(len(write_lines) - 1):
   223→                first, second = write_lines[idx], write_lines[idx + 1]
   224→                has_read_between = any(first < read <= second for read in read_lines)
   225→                if not has_read_between:
   226→                    issues.append(
   227→                        {
   228→                            "file": visitor.filepath,
   229→                            "kind": "overwritten_key",
   230→                            "variable": tracked.name,
   231→                            "key": key,
   232→                            "line": second,
   233→                            "func": func_name,
   234→                            "tier": 3,
   235→                            "confidence": "medium",
   236→                            "summary": (
   237→                                f'Dict key "{key}" overwritten on `{tracked.name}` '
   238→                                f"at line {second} (previously set at line {first}, "
   239→                                "never read between)"
   240→                            ),
   241→                            "detail": f"in {func_name}()",
   242→                        }
   243→                    )
   244→    return issues

   246→
   247→class DictKeyVisitor(ast.NodeVisitor):
   248→    """Walk a module AST, tracking dict key writes/reads per function scope."""
   249→
   250→    def __init__(self, filepath: str):
   251→        self.filepath = filepath
   252→        self._scopes: list[dict[str, TrackedDict]] = []
   253→        self._class_dicts: dict[str, TrackedDict] = {}  # self.x dicts
   254→        self._in_init_or_setup = False
   255→        self._issues: list[dict] = []
   256→        self._dict_literals: list[dict] = []  # for schema drift
   257→
   258→    def _current_scope(self) -> dict[str, TrackedDict]:
   259→        return self._scopes[-1] if self._scopes else {}
   260→
   261→    def _track(
   262→        self,
   263→        name: str,
   264→        line: int,
   265→        *,
   266→        locally_created: bool,
   267→        initial_keys: list[str] | None = None,
   268→    ) -> TrackedDict:
   269→        scope = self._current_scope()
   270→        td = TrackedDict(name=name, created_line=line, locally_created=locally_created)
   271→        if initial_keys:
   272→            for k in initial_keys:
   273→                td.writes[k].append(line)
   274→        scope[name] = td
   275→        return td
   276→
   277→    def _get_tracked(self, name: str) -> TrackedDict | None:
   278→        # Check current scope first, then class scope for self.x
   279→        for scope in reversed(self._scopes):
   280→            if name in scope:
   281→                return scope[name]
   282→        if name.startswith("self.") and name in self._class_dicts:
   283→            return self._class_dicts[name]
   284→        return None
   285→
   286→    # -- Scope management --
   287→
   288→    def visit_FunctionDef(self, node: ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
   289→        prev_init = self._in_init_or_setup
   290→        self._in_init_or_setup = node.name in ("__init__", "setUp", "setup")
   291→        self._scopes.append({})
   292→        self.generic_visit(node)
   293→        scope = self._scopes.pop()
   294→        self._issues.extend(_analyze_scope_issues(self, scope, node.name))
   295→        self._in_init_or_setup = prev_init
   296→
   297→    visit_AsyncFunctionDef = visit_FunctionDef
   298→
   299→    def visit_ClassDef(self, node: ast.ClassDef) -> None:
   300→        prev_class_dicts = self._class_dicts
   301→        self._class_dicts = {}
   302→        self.generic_visit(node)
   303→        self._issues.extend(
   304→            _analyze_scope_issues(
   305→                self,
   306→                self._class_dicts,
   307→                f"class {node.name}",
   308→                is_class=True,
   309→            )
   310→        )
   311→        self._class_dicts = prev_class_dicts
   312→
   313→    # -- Dict creation --
   314→
   315→    def visit_Assign(self, node: ast.Assign) -> None:
   316→        if len(node.targets) == 1:
   317→            target = node.targets[0]
   318→            name = _get_name(target)
   319→            if name:
   320→                self._check_dict_creation(name, node.value, node.lineno)
   321→        # Also check for subscript writes: d["key"] = val
   322→        for target in node.targets:
   323→            self._check_subscript_write(target, node.lineno)
   324→        _mark_assignment_escape(self, node.targets, node.value)
   325→        self.generic_visit(node)
   326→
   327→    def visit_AugAssign(self, node: ast.AugAssign) -> None:
   328→        # AugAssign (d["k"] += v) is both a read AND a write
   329→        if isinstance(node.target, ast.Subscript):
   330→            name = _get_name(node.target.value)
   331→            if name:
   332→                td = self._get_tracked(name)
   333→                if td:
   334→                    key = _get_str_key(node.target.slice)
   335→                    if key:
   336→                        td.reads[key].append(node.lineno)
   337→                    else:
   338→                        td.has_dynamic_key = True
   339→        self._check_subscript_write(node.target, node.lineno)
   340→        self.generic_visit(node)
   341→
   342→    def _check_dict_creation(self, name: str, value: ast.expr, line: int):
   343→        """Detect d = {}, d = dict(), d = {"k": v, ...}."""
   344→        initial_keys: list[str] = []
   345→        is_creation = False
   346→
   347→        if isinstance(value, ast.Dict):
   348→            is_creation = True
   349→            for k in value.keys:
   350→                sk = _get_str_key(k) if k else None
   351→                if sk:
   352→                    initial_keys.append(sk)
   353→            # Collect dict literal for schema drift
   354→            if (
   355→                all(
   356→                    isinstance(k, ast.Constant) and isinstance(k.value, str)
   357→                    for k in value.keys
   358→                    if k is not None
   359→                )
   360→                and len(value.keys) >= 3
   361→            ):
   362→                keys = [k.value for k in value.keys if isinstance(k, ast.Constant)]
   363→                self._dict_literals.append(
   364→                    {
   365→                        "file": self.filepath,
   366→                        "line": line,
   367→                        "keys": frozenset(keys),
   368→                    }
   369→                )
   370→        elif (
   371→            isinstance(value, ast.Call)
   372→            and isinstance(value.func, ast.Name)
   373→            and value.func.id == "dict"
   374→        ):
   375→            is_creation = True
   376→            for kw in value.keywords:
   377→                if kw.arg:
   378→                    initial_keys.append(kw.arg)
   379→
   380→        if is_creation:
   381→            td = self._track(
   382→                name, line, locally_created=True, initial_keys=initial_keys
   383→            )
   384→            # Store as class dict if it's self.x
   385→            if name.startswith("self.") and self._in_init_or_setup:
   386→                self._class_dicts[name] = td
   387→
   388→    def _check_subscript_write(self, target: ast.expr, line: int):
   389→        """Handle d["key"] = val or d["key"] += val."""
   390→        if not isinstance(target, ast.Subscript):
   391→            return
   392→        name = _get_name(target.value)
   393→        if not name:
   394→            return
   395→        key = _get_str_key(target.slice)
   396→        td = self._get_tracked(name)
   397→        if td is None:
   398→            return
   399→        if key:
   400→            td.writes[key].append(line)
   401→        else:
   402→            td.has_dynamic_key = True
   403→
   404→    # -- Dict reads --
   405→
   406→    def visit_Subscript(self, node: ast.Subscript) -> None:
   407→        if isinstance(node.ctx, ast.Load):
   408→            name = _get_name(node.value)
   409→            if name:
   410→                td = self._get_tracked(name)
   411→                if td:
   412→                    key = _get_str_key(node.slice)
   413→                    if key:
   414→                        td.reads[key].append(node.lineno)
   415→                    else:
   416→                        td.has_dynamic_key = True
   417→        self.generic_visit(node)
   418→
   419→    def visit_Delete(self, node: ast.Delete) -> None:
   420→        for target in node.targets:
   421→            if isinstance(target, ast.Subscript):
   422→                name = _get_name(target.value)
   423→                if name:
   424→                    td = self._get_tracked(name)
   425→                    if td:
   426→                        key = _get_str_key(target.slice)
   427→                        if key:
   428→                            td.reads[key].append(target.lineno)
   429→                        else:
   430→                            td.has_dynamic_key = True
   431→        self.generic_visit(node)
   432→
   433→    def visit_Call(self, node: ast.Call) -> None:
   434→        _record_call_interactions(self, node)
   435→        self.generic_visit(node)
   436→
   437→    def visit_Return(self, node: ast.Return):
   438→        if node.value:
   439→            _mark_returned_or_passed(self, node.value)
   440→        self.generic_visit(node)
   441→
   442→    visit_Yield = visit_Return
   443→    visit_YieldFrom = visit_Return
   444→
   445→    def visit_Compare(self, node: ast.Compare) -> None:
   446→        """Handle "key" in d."""
   447→        for i, op in enumerate(node.ops):
   448→            if isinstance(op, ast.In | ast.NotIn):
   449→                comparator = node.comparators[i]
   450→                name = _get_name(comparator)
   451→                if name:
   452→                    td = self._get_tracked(name)
   453→                    if td:
   454→                        # The left side of `in` for the first op is node.left
   455→                        left = node.left if i == 0 else node.comparators[i - 1]
   456→                        key = _get_str_key(left)
   457→                        if key:
   458→                            td.reads[key].append(node.lineno)
   459→        self.generic_visit(node)
   460→
   461→    def visit_For(self, node: ast.For):
   462→        """Handle `for x in d` — bulk read."""
   463→        name = _get_name(node.iter)
   464→        if name:
   465→            td = self._get_tracked(name)
   466→            if td:
   467→                td.bulk_read = True
   468→        self.generic_visit(node)
   469→
   470→    def visit_Starred(self, node: ast.Starred):
   471→        """Handle {**d} or func(*d)."""
   472→        name = _get_name(node.value)
   473→        if name:
   474→            td = self._get_tracked(name)
   475→            if td:
   476→                td.has_star_unpack = True
   477→        self.generic_visit(node)
   478→
   479→    # -- Dict literal collection (standalone, non-assigned) --
   480→
   481→    def visit_Dict(self, node: ast.Dict) -> None:
   482→        """Collect dict literals for schema drift analysis."""
   483→        if (
   484→            all(
   485→                isinstance(k, ast.Constant) and isinstance(k.value, str)
   486→                for k in node.keys
   487→                if k is not None
   488→            )
   489→            and len(node.keys) >= 3
   490→            and all(k is not None for k in node.keys)
   491→        ):
   492→            keys = frozenset(k.value for k in node.keys if isinstance(k, ast.Constant))
   493→            self._dict_literals.append(
   494→                {
   495→                    "file": self.filepath,
   496→                    "line": node.lineno,
   497→                    "keys": keys,
   498→                }
   499→            )
   500→        self.generic_visit(node)
   501→

1→"""Review import cache refresh helpers."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from pathlib import Path
     6→from typing import Any
     7→
     8→from desloppify.core.text.text_api import get_project_root
     9→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel
    10→from desloppify.intelligence.review.importing.state_helpers import _review_file_cache
    11→from desloppify.state import utc_now
    12→
    13→
    14→def resolve_import_project_root(project_root: Path | str | None) -> Path:
    15→    """Resolve optional import project root to an absolute path."""
    16→    if project_root is None:
    17→        return get_project_root()
    18→    return Path(project_root).resolve()
    19→
    20→
    21→def upsert_review_cache_entry(
    22→    file_cache: dict[str, Any],
    23→    file_path: str,
    24→    *,
    25→    project_root: Path,
    26→    hash_file_fn,
    27→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
    28→    issue_count: int | None = None,
    29→) -> None:
    30→    """Write one normalized review-cache entry for a reviewed file."""
    31→    absolute = project_root / file_path
    32→    content_hash = hash_file_fn(str(absolute)) if absolute.exists() else ""
    33→    if issue_count is None:
    34→        previous = file_cache.get(file_path, {})
    35→        count = previous.get("issue_count", 0) if isinstance(previous, dict) else 0
    36→        issue_count = count if isinstance(count, int) else 0
    37→    file_cache[file_path] = {
    38→        "content_hash": content_hash,
    39→        "reviewed_at": utc_now_fn(),
    40→        "issue_count": max(0, int(issue_count)),
    41→    }
    42→
    43→
    44→def refresh_review_file_cache(
    45→    state: StateModel,
    46→    *,
    47→    reviewed_files: list[str] | None,
    48→    issues_by_file: dict[str, int | None] | None = None,
    49→    project_root: Path | str | None = None,
    50→    hash_file_fn,
    51→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
    52→) -> None:
    53→    """Refresh normalized review cache entries for all reviewed files."""
    54→    file_cache = _review_file_cache(state)
    55→    resolved_project_root = resolve_import_project_root(project_root)
    56→    counts = issues_by_file or {}
    57→
    58→    reviewed_set = set(counts)
    59→    if reviewed_files:
    60→        reviewed_set.update(

    97→        if issue_errors:

   394→def _resolve_total_files(state: StateModel, lang_name: str | None) -> int:
   395→    """Best-effort total file count from codebase_metrics or review cache."""
   396→    review_cache = state.get("review_cache", {})
   397→    fallback = len(review_cache.get("files", {}))
   398→
   399→    codebase_metrics = state.get("codebase_metrics", {})
   400→    if not isinstance(codebase_metrics, dict):
   401→        return fallback
   402→
   403→    # Try language-specific metrics first, then global.
   404→    sources = []
   405→    if lang_name:
   406→        lang_metrics = codebase_metrics.get(lang_name)
   407→        if isinstance(lang_metrics, dict):
   408→            sources.append(lang_metrics)
   409→    sources.append(codebase_metrics)
   410→
   411→    for source in sources:
   412→        metric_total = source.get("total_files")
   413→        if isinstance(metric_total, int) and metric_total > 0:
   414→            return metric_total
   415→
   416→    return fallback
   417→
   418→
   419→def update_holistic_review_cache(
   420→    state: StateModel,
   421→    issues_data: list[dict],
   422→    *,
   423→    lang_name: str | None = None,
   424→    review_scope: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   425→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
   426→) -> None:
   427→    """Store holistic review metadata in review_cache."""
   428→    review_cache = state.setdefault("review_cache", {})
   429→    now = utc_now_fn()
   430→    _, holistic_prompts, _ = load_dimensions_for_lang(lang_name or "")
   431→
   432→    valid = [
   433→        issue
   434→        for issue in issues_data
   435→        if all(
   436→            key in issue
   437→            for key in ("dimension", "identifier", "summary", "confidence")
   438→        )
   439→        and issue["dimension"] in holistic_prompts
   440→    ]
   441→
   442→    resolved_total_files: int
   443→    total_override = (
   444→        review_scope.get("total_files")
   445→        if isinstance(review_scope, dict)
   446→        else None
   447→    )
   448→    if (
   449→        isinstance(total_override, int)
   450→        and not isinstance(total_override, bool)
   451→        and total_override > 0
   452→    ):
   453→        resolved_total_files = total_override
   454→    else:
   455→        resolved_total_files = _resolve_total_files(state, lang_name)
   456→
   457→    holistic_entry: dict[str, Any] = {
   458→        "reviewed_at": now,
   459→        "file_count_at_review": resolved_total_files,
   460→        "issue_count": len(valid),
   461→    }
   462→    if isinstance(review_scope, dict):
   463→        reviewed_files_count = review_scope.get("reviewed_files_count")
   464→        if (
   465→            isinstance(reviewed_files_count, int)
   466→            and not isinstance(reviewed_files_count, bool)
   467→            and reviewed_files_count >= 0
   468→        ):
   469→            holistic_entry["reviewed_files_count"] = reviewed_files_count
   470→        full_sweep_included = review_scope.get("full_sweep_included")
   471→        if isinstance(full_sweep_included, bool):
   472→            holistic_entry["full_sweep_included"] = full_sweep_included
   473→
   474→    review_cache["holistic"] = holistic_entry
   475→
   476→
   477→def resolve_holistic_coverage_issues(
   478→    state: StateModel,
   479→    diff: dict[str, Any],
   480→    *,
   481→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
   482→) -> None:
   483→    """Resolve stale holistic coverage entries after successful holistic import."""
   484→    now = utc_now_fn()
   485→    for issue in state.get("issues", {}).values():
   486→        if issue.get("status") != "open":
   487→            continue
   488→        if issue.get("detector") != "subjective_review":
   489→            continue
   490→
   491→        issue_id = issue.get("id", "")
   492→        if (
   493→            "::holistic_unreviewed" not in issue_id
   494→            and "::holistic_stale" not in issue_id
   495→        ):
   496→            continue
   497→
   498→        issue["status"] = "auto_resolved"
   499→        issue["resolved_at"] = now
   500→        issue["note"] = "resolved by holistic review import"
   501→        issue["resolution_attestation"] = {
   502→            "kind": "agent_import",
   503→            "text": "Holistic review refreshed; coverage marker superseded",
   504→            "attested_at": now,
   505→            "scan_verified": False,
   506→        }
   507→        diff["auto_resolved"] += 1
   508→
   509→
   510→def resolve_reviewed_file_coverage_issues(
   511→    state: StateModel,
   512→    diff: dict[str, Any],
   513→    reviewed_files: list[str],
   514→    *,
   515→    utc_now_fn=utc_now,
   516→) -> None:
   517→    """Resolve per-file subjective coverage markers for freshly reviewed files."""
   518→    if not reviewed_files:

   520→
   521→    reviewed_set = {path for path in reviewed_files if isinstance(path, str) and path}
   522→    if not reviewed_set:
   523→        return

   526→    for issue in state.get("issues", {}).values():

    61→class ReviewPrepareOptions:
